162	        description="Direct snippet, quote, or summarized information found in the sources regarding the claim"
163	    )
164	    source_url: str = Field(description="The exact URL of the source for this claim")
165	    source_title: str = Field(description="The title of the source page/article")
166	    evidence_type: Literal["fetched_page", "search_snippet"] = Field(
167	        description="Must be 'fetched_page' ONLY if content was successfully retrieved via fetch_page tool; otherwise 'search_snippet'"
168	    )
169	    verification_status: Literal["unverified", "fetched", "audited_supported", "audited_contradicted", "failed"] = Field(
170	        description="'unverified' if based only on search snippet, 'fetched' if retrieved via successful fetch_page, 'audited_supported'/'audited_contradicted' after auditor evaluation, 'failed' if fetch failed"
171	    )
172	
173	class ClaimsExtraction(BaseModel):
174	    claims: List[Claim]
175	
176	class AuditRecord(BaseModel):
177	    original_claim: str = Field(description="The original user claim evaluated by the Auditor")
178	    source_url: str = Field(description="The cited source URL")
179	    evidence_type: Literal["fetched_page", "search_snippet"] = Field(
180	        description="The evidence type of the claim ('fetched_page' or 'search_snippet')"
181	    )
182	    verification_status: Literal["unverified", "fetched", "audited_supported", "audited_contradicted", "failed"] = Field(
183	        description="The updated verification status after auditor evaluation"
184	    )
185	    verdict: Literal["supported", "unsupported", "contradicted"] = Field(
186	        description="Must be 'supported' if cited source actually supports original_claim, 'contradicted' if source directly conflicts with original_claim, or 'unsupported' if source lacks sufficient evidence or fetch failed"
187	    )
188	    reasoning: str = Field(description="Independent audit reasoning explaining the verdict for the original claim")
189	    supporting_evidence: str = Field(
190	        description="Direct text snippet/excerpt quote extracted from the independently fetched source page, or explanation if unavailable"
191	    )
192	
193	class ResearchLesson(BaseModel):
194	    lesson: str = Field(description="Concise, actionable rule/directive to improve future research")
195	    reason: str = Field(description="Explanation of why this lesson was derived from the audit results")
196	    source_of_feedback: Literal["auditor"] = Field(default="auditor", description="Source of feedback, set to 'auditor'")
197	
198	class FeedbackOutput(BaseModel):
199	    lessons: List[ResearchLesson]
200	
201	class State(TypedDict):
202	    # `add_messages` appends new messages to the existing list rather than overwriting them
203	    messages: Annotated[list, add_messages]
204	    claims: list[dict]
205	    audit_results: list[dict]
206	    feedback_lessons: list[dict]

208	# 3. Initialize model and bind tools
209	tools = [calculator, web_search, fetch_page]
210	llm = ChatGoogleGenerativeAI(model="gemini-3.5-flash-lite", temperature=0)

213	BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
214	    "You are a meticulous research analyst assistant.\n"
215	    "When answering user queries using your tools, strictly follow these evidence rules:\n"
216	    "1. When performing web searches, preserve and use exact URLs returned by the search tool.\n"
217	    "2. If fetch_page is not executed or fails (returns `[FETCH STATUS: FAILED]`), DO NOT describe that evidence as fetched or verified. You MUST explicitly state that the source page could not be independently fetched/verified.\n"
218	    "3. Categorize all information in your response strictly using ONLY the following language labels:\n"
219	    "   - Use 'Information from Search Snippets' for any evidence obtained via web_search where fetch_page was not run or failed.\n"
220	    "   - Use 'Information from Fetched Page Content' ONLY when fetch_page actually succeeded and returned page content.\n"
221	    "   - Use 'Auditor-verified evidence' ONLY if the Auditor successfully fetched the source page and produced a supported or contradicted verdict.\n"
222	    "4. NEVER describe search snippet evidence or failed page fetches as 'verified' or 'verified from fetched page content'.\n"
223	    "5. NEVER infer or claim that a search result is verified merely because the URL points to a primary source (e.g. SEC.gov, EDGAR, government domains, official corporate sites).\n"
224	    "6. If a calculation was performed, include the calculation details."
225	)

227	# 4. Define Graph Nodes
228	def analyze_tool_history(messages: list) -> dict:
229	    """Scans message history for tool calls and outputs deterministic evidence status per URL."""
230	    successfully_fetched = set()
231	    failed_fetched = set()
232	    search_snippet_urls = set()
233	
234	    for msg in messages:
235	        if hasattr(msg, "type") and msg.type == "tool":
236	            content = str(msg.content)
237	            if "[FETCH STATUS: SUCCESS]" in content:
238	                for line in content.split("\n"):
239	                    if line.startswith("URL:"):
240	                        url = line.replace("URL:", "").strip()
241	                        if url:
242	                            successfully_fetched.add(url)
243	            elif "[FETCH STATUS: FAILED]" in content:
244	                for line in content.split("\n"):
245	                    if line.startswith("URL:"):
246	                        url = line.replace("URL:", "").strip()
247	                        if url:
248	                            failed_fetched.add(url)
249	            elif "URL:" in content or "http" in content:
250	                for line in content.split("\n"):
251	                    if line.startswith("URL:"):
252	                        url = line.replace("URL:", "").strip()
253	                        if url:
254	                            search_snippet_urls.add(url)
255	
256	    unverified_urls = (search_snippet_urls | failed_fetched) - successfully_fetched
257	
258	    return {
259	        "successfully_fetched": list(successfully_fetched),
260	        "unverified_urls": list(unverified_urls)
261	    }
262	
263	def chatbot(state: State):
264	    """The main LLM node that decides whether to answer or call a tool, incorporating learned research memory lessons."""
265	    memory_lessons = load_memory()
266	    tool_status = analyze_tool_history(state["messages"])
267	    
268	    # Construct evidence manifest for response synthesis
269	    if tool_status["successfully_fetched"] or tool_status["unverified_urls"]:
270	        fetched_str = "\n".join(f"- {u}" for u in tool_status["successfully_fetched"]) if tool_status["successfully_fetched"] else "- None"
271	        unverified_str = "\n".join(f"- {u}" for u in tool_status["unverified_urls"]) if tool_status["unverified_urls"] else "- None"
272	        
273	        manifest_section = (
274	            f"\n\n### DETERMINISTIC EVIDENCE STATUS MANIFEST (STRICT COMPLIANCE REQUIRED):\n"
275	            f"1. SUCCESSFULLY FETCHED URLs:\n{fetched_str}\n"
276	            f"   (ONLY content from these exact URLs may be described under 'Information from Fetched Page Content'.)\n\n"
277	            f"2. UNVERIFIED / FAILED FETCH URLs:\n{unverified_str}\n"
278	            f"   (Content from these URLs MUST ONLY be described under 'Information from Search Snippets'. You MUST explicitly state that these source pages could not be independently fetched/verified.)\n\n"
279	            f"STRICT RULES:\n"
280	            f"- If a source URL is under 'UNVERIFIED / FAILED FETCH URLs', NEVER describe it under 'Information from Fetched Page Content', even if it is a primary domain (e.g. SEC.gov, EDGAR, GuruFocus, Microsoft.com).\n"
281	            f"- If 'SUCCESSFULLY FETCHED URLs' is None, list '*None*' under 'Information from Fetched Page Content'."
282	        )
283	    else:
284	        manifest_section = ""
285	
286	    if memory_lessons:
287	        lessons_formatted = "\n".join(
288	            f"- {item['lesson']} (Reason: {item['reason']})" for item in memory_lessons
289	        )
290	        system_content = (
291	            f"{BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT}{manifest_section}\n\n"
292	            f"### RELEVANT LESSONS FROM PREVIOUS AUDITS:\n"
293	            f"Follow these guidelines derived from past audit feedback:\n"
294	            f"{lessons_formatted}"
295	        )
296	    else:
297	        system_content = f"{BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT}{manifest_section}"
298	
299	    messages = [SystemMessage(content=system_content)] + state["messages"]
300	    return {"messages": [llm_with_tools.invoke(messages)]}

302	def extract_claims(state: State):
303	    """Parses conversation history into structured claims and updates the graph state."""
304	    structured_llm = llm.with_structured_output(ClaimsExtraction)
305	    extraction_prompt = (
306	        "Analyze the entire conversation history above. Extract factual research claims into structured records.\n"
307	        "Follow these strict rules:\n"
308	        "1. Set 'original_claim' to the EXACT statement, question, or assertion made by the user in their input message. NEVER rewrite, modify, or correct 'original_claim' based on research findings or search evidence.\n"
309	        "2. Set 'evidence' to the snippet, quote, or information found in search/fetch results.\n"
310	        "3. Set 'evidence_type' to 'fetched_page' ONLY if content comes from a successful `fetch_page` tool call in history; otherwise set to 'search_snippet'.\n"
311	        "4. Set 'verification_status' strictly based on evidence source:\n"
312	        "   - Set to 'fetched' if content comes from a successful `fetch_page` tool call.\n"
313	        "   - Set to 'failed' if a `fetch_page` call was attempted but failed/returned `[FETCH STATUS: FAILED]`.\n"
314	        "   - Set to 'unverified' if based only on web_search snippets without a successful fetch."
315	    )
316	    messages = state["messages"] + [HumanMessage(content=extraction_prompt)]
317	    try:
318	        result = structured_llm.invoke(messages)
319	        extracted = [claim.model_dump() for claim in result.claims] if result and result.claims else []
320	    except Exception as e:
321	        extracted = []
322	    return {"claims": extracted}

324	def auditor(state: State):
325	    """Independently evaluates each extracted Analyst claim by re-inspecting cited sources."""
326	    claims = state.get("claims", [])
327	    if not claims:
328	        return {"audit_results": [], "claims": []}
329	
330	    audit_results = []
331	    updated_claims = []
332	    structured_auditor = llm.with_structured_output(AuditRecord)
333	
334	    for claim in claims:
335	        claim_copy = dict(claim)
336	        original_claim = claim_copy.get("original_claim", "")
337	        source_url = claim_copy.get("source_url", "")
338	        evidence_type = claim_copy.get("evidence_type", "search_snippet")
339	        
340	        print(f"\nAUDITOR -> fetching {source_url if source_url else '<No URL>'}")
341	        
342	        # Independently fetch the cited source page
343	        if source_url and source_url != "No URL":
344	            try:
345	                fetched_data = fetch_page.invoke({"url": source_url})
346	            except Exception as e:
347	                fetched_data = f"[FETCH STATUS: FAILED]\nURL: {source_url}\nREASON: Exception during fetch ({str(e)})"
348	        else:
349	            fetched_data = "[FETCH STATUS: FAILED]\nURL: None\nREASON: No source URL provided by Analyst."
350	
351	        if fetched_data.startswith("[FETCH STATUS: FAILED]"):
352	            verdict = "unsupported"
353	            verification_status = "failed"
354	            reasoning = f"Independent page fetch failed for URL '{source_url}'. The original claim cannot be verified without accessible source page content."
355	            supporting_evidence = fetched_data
356	
357	            print(f"AUDITOR -> fetch failed: {source_url if source_url else '<No URL>'}")
358	            print(f"AUDITOR -> verdict: UNSUPPORTED | evidence_type: {evidence_type} | verification_status: {verification_status}")
359	            
360	            record = {
361	                "original_claim": original_claim,
362	                "source_url": source_url,
363	                "evidence_type": evidence_type,
364	                "verification_status": verification_status,
365	                "verdict": verdict,
366	                "reasoning": reasoning,
367	                "supporting_evidence": supporting_evidence
368	            }
369	            audit_results.append(record)
370	            claim_copy["verification_status"] = verification_status
371	            updated_claims.append(claim_copy)
372	        else:
373	            print(f"AUDITOR -> fetch succeeded: {source_url}")
374	            audit_prompt = (
375	                f"You are an independent Auditor performing zero-trust verification of an ORIGINAL user claim.\n\n"
376	                f"ORIGINAL CLAIM TO EVALUATE:\n\"{original_claim}\"\n\n"
377	                f"CITED SOURCE URL:\n{source_url}\n\n"
378	                f"INDEPENDENTLY FETCHED SOURCE PAGE CONTENT:\n{fetched_data[:8000]}\n\n"
379	                f"STRICT RULES:\n"
380	                f"1. Base your verdict EXCLUSIVELY on the INDEPENDENTLY FETCHED SOURCE PAGE CONTENT provided above.\n"
381	                f"2. Do NOT evaluate based on search snippets, memory, or external assumptions.\n"
382	                f"3. Assign verdict='supported' ONLY if the fetched page content explicitly and directly verifies the original claim.\n"
383	                f"4. Assign verdict='contradicted' if the fetched page content directly refutes or contradicts the original claim (e.g. claim states 2010 but fetched page states 2014).\n"
384	                f"5. Assign verdict='unsupported' if the fetched page content does not contain sufficient facts to verify or disprove the original claim.\n"
385	                f"6. Do NOT invent or fabricate evidence. In supporting_evidence, extract direct quote excerpts directly from the fetched page content."
386	            )
387	            try:
388	                res = structured_auditor.invoke([HumanMessage(content=audit_prompt)])
389	                if res:
390	                    verdict = res.verdict
391	                    if verdict == "supported":
392	                        verification_status = "audited_supported"
393	                    elif verdict == "contradicted":
394	                        verification_status = "audited_contradicted"
395	                    else:
396	                        verification_status = "failed"
397	                    
398	                    print(f"AUDITOR -> verdict: {verdict.upper()} | evidence_type: {evidence_type} | verification_status: {verification_status}")
399	                    
400	                    record = res.model_dump()
401	                    record["evidence_type"] = evidence_type
402	                    record["verification_status"] = verification_status
403	                    audit_results.append(record)
404	                    claim_copy["verification_status"] = verification_status
405	                    updated_claims.append(claim_copy)
406	                else:
407	                    verdict = "unsupported"
408	                    verification_status = "failed"
409	                    print(f"AUDITOR -> verdict: UNSUPPORTED (Empty Response) | evidence_type: {evidence_type} | verification_status: {verification_status}")
410	                    record = {
411	                        "original_claim": original_claim,
412	                        "source_url": source_url,
413	                        "evidence_type": evidence_type,
414	                        "verification_status": verification_status,
415	                        "verdict": verdict,
416	                        "reasoning": "Auditor model returned empty evaluation response.",
417	                        "supporting_evidence": "None"
418	                    }
419	                    audit_results.append(record)
420	                    claim_copy["verification_status"] = verification_status
421	                    updated_claims.append(claim_copy)
422	            except Exception as e:
423	                verdict = "unsupported"
424	                verification_status = "failed"
425	                print(f"AUDITOR -> verdict: UNSUPPORTED (Exception) | evidence_type: {evidence_type} | verification_status: {verification_status}")
426	                record = {
427	                    "original_claim": original_claim,
428	                    "source_url": source_url,
429	                    "evidence_type": evidence_type,
430	                    "verification_status": verification_status,
431	                    "verdict": verdict,
432	                    "reasoning": f"Auditor evaluation error: {str(e)}",
433	                    "supporting_evidence": "None"
434	                }
435	                audit_results.append(record)
436	                claim_copy["verification_status"] = verification_status
437	                updated_claims.append(claim_copy)
438	
439	    print("\n[VALIDATION DEBUG CHECK - EVIDENCE & AUDIT SUMMARY]:")
440	    for idx, (c, a) in enumerate(zip(updated_claims, audit_results), 1):
441	        print(f"  Record {idx}:")
442	        print(f"    - Source URL: {c.get('source_url', 'No URL')}")
443	        print(f"    - Evidence Type: {c.get('evidence_type', 'unknown')}")
444	        print(f"    - Verification Status: {c.get('verification_status', 'unknown')}")
445	        print(f"    - Auditor Verdict: {a.get('verdict', 'unknown').upper()}")
446	
447	    return {"audit_results": audit_results, "claims": updated_claims}

449	def feedback(state: State):
450	    """Analyzes audit_results and claims to generate persistent research lessons that improve future Analyst runs."""
451	    audit_results = state.get("audit_results", [])
452	    claims = state.get("claims", [])
453	
454	    print(f"\n[Feedback Engine Debug]: Received {len(audit_results)} audit result(s) and {len(claims)} claim(s).")
455	    
456	    if not audit_results and not claims:
457	        print("[Feedback Engine Debug Summary]: No audit results or claims received.")
458	        return {"feedback_lessons": []}
459	
460	    combined_context = []
461	    for idx, audit in enumerate(audit_results):
462	        matching_claim = next((c for c in claims if c.get("original_claim") == audit.get("original_claim")), None)
463	        if not matching_claim and idx < len(claims):
464	            matching_claim = claims[idx]
465	            
466	        ctx = {
467	            "original_claim": audit.get("original_claim", ""),
468	            "auditor_verdict": audit.get("verdict", ""),
469	            "auditor_reasoning": audit.get("reasoning", ""),
470	            "supporting_evidence": audit.get("supporting_evidence", ""),
471	            "source_url": audit.get("source_url", ""),
472	            "evidence_type": matching_claim.get("evidence_type", "unknown") if matching_claim else "unknown",
473	            "verification_status": matching_claim.get("verification_status", "unknown") if matching_claim else "unknown",
474	            "analyst_evidence": matching_claim.get("evidence", "") if matching_claim else ""
475	        }
476	        combined_context.append(ctx)
477	
478	    existing_lessons = load_memory()
479	    existing_lessons_text = "\n".join([f"- {l['lesson']}" for l in existing_lessons]) if existing_lessons else "None"
480	
481	    structured_feedback = llm.with_structured_output(FeedbackOutput)
482	    
483	    prompt = (
484	        "You are the Research Feedback Engine. Analyze the following combined research claims and audit verification results:\n\n"
485	        f"AUDIT CONTEXT:\n{json.dumps(combined_context, indent=2)}\n\n"
486	        f"EXISTING LESSONS ALREADY IN MEMORY:\n{existing_lessons_text}\n\n"
487	        "YOUR TASK:\n"
488	        "Identify specific shortcomings, verification failures, or areas for improvement in the Analyst's research.\n"
489	        "Generate NEW concise, actionable research lessons for future Analyst runs.\n\n"
490	        "TRIGGER CRITERIA FOR GENERATING A LESSON:\n"
491	        "1. verdict == 'unsupported'\n"
492	        "2. verdict == 'contradicted'\n"
493	        "3. source fetch failed (e.g. 400 error, HTTP failure, unreachable URL)\n"
494	        "4. analyst relied on search_snippet instead of fetching the page (evidence_type == 'search_snippet')\n"
495	        "5. specific factual, numerical, percentage, or date assertions made without primary source verification\n\n"
496	        "RULES:\n"
497	        "- Do NOT generate exact duplicate lessons of those already listed under EXISTING LESSONS ALREADY IN MEMORY.\n"
498	        "- If an existing lesson is general (e.g. 'Prefer sources that can be independently fetched.'), but the current failure involves specific issues like search snippet reliance, unverified percentage assertions, or unverified claims, generate a NEW, distinct actionable lesson (e.g., 'Verify specific ownership percentages and financial claims against primary sources before asserting exact metrics.').\n"
499	        "- Set 'source_of_feedback' to 'auditor' for all lessons.\n"
500	        "- If all claims are fully supported and verified with fetched pages, return an empty list of lessons."
501	    )
502	    
503	    try:
504	        result = structured_feedback.invoke([HumanMessage(content=prompt)])
505	        new_lessons = [l.model_dump() for l in result.lessons] if result and result.lessons else []
506	    except Exception as e:
507	        print(f"FEEDBACK -> Exception during feedback generation: {e}")
508	        new_lessons = []
509	
510	    added, duplicates = add_lessons_to_memory(new_lessons)
511	    
512	    print(f"\n[Feedback Engine Debug Summary]:")
513	    print(f"  - Audit results received: {len(audit_results)}")
514	    print(f"  - Claims received: {len(claims)}")
515	    print(f"  - Total lessons generated by LLM: {len(new_lessons)}")
516	    for idx, item in enumerate(new_lessons, 1):
517	        is_dup = any(item.get("lesson", "").strip().lower() == d.get("lesson", "").strip().lower() for d in duplicates)
518	        status_str = "DUPLICATE (ignored)" if is_dup else "NEW (added to memory)"
519	        print(f"    {idx}. [{status_str}] Lesson: {item.get('lesson', '')}")
520	        print(f"       Reason: {item.get('reason', '')}")
521	        print(f"       Source of Feedback: {item.get('source_of_feedback', 'auditor')}")
522	
523	    return {"feedback_lessons": added}

525	def route_after_chatbot(state: State):
526	    """Routes to tools node if tool call exists; otherwise routes to extract_claims node."""
527	    route = tools_condition(state)
528	    if route == END:
529	        return "extract_claims"
530	    return route

532	# 5. Build the Agent Graph
533	graph_builder = StateGraph(State)
534	
535	# Add nodes
536	graph_builder.add_node("chatbot", chatbot)
537	tool_node = ToolNode(tools=tools)
538	graph_builder.add_node("tools", tool_node)
539	graph_builder.add_node("extract_claims", extract_claims)
540	graph_builder.add_node("auditor", auditor)
541	graph_builder.add_node("feedback", feedback)
542	
543	# Define edges
544	graph_builder.add_edge(START, "chatbot")
545	
546	graph_builder.add_conditional_edges(
547	    "chatbot",
548	    route_after_chatbot,
549	    {"tools": "tools", "extract_claims": "extract_claims"}
550	)
551	graph_builder.add_edge("tools", "chatbot")
552	graph_builder.add_edge("extract_claims", "auditor")
553	graph_builder.add_edge("auditor", "feedback")
554	graph_builder.add_edge("feedback", END)
555	
556	# Compile graph
557	agent = graph_builder.compile()
558	
559	if __name__ == "__main__":

- **`chatbot()`** (lines 263‑300): calls `analyze_tool_history` and injects a `DETERMINISTIC EVIDENCE STATUS MANIFEST` block into the system prompt, instructing the LLM which URLs it may call "Fetched Page Content" vs must call "Search Snippets," with "STRICT COMPLIANCE REQUIRED" language.
- **`auditor()`** (lines 439‑445): added a debug `print` block dumping claim/audit records per iteration — cosmetic, no logic change.

**3. Is the Phase 6.1 bug fixed? No.**

The fix is incomplete and doesn't actually solve the stated problem:

- **Wrong layer, and still LLM-dependent.** The manifest only *asks* the LLM (via prompt instructions) to label things correctly. It's not a deterministic derivation from structured state — it's a stronger prompt, which the task explicitly rules out ("final answer must derive evidence labels from structured state, not LLM-generated assumptions").
- **Architecturally can't cover the Auditor label at all.** The user-visible final answer is produced entirely inside `chatbot()`, and `route_after_chatbot` only proceeds to `extract_claims → auditor → feedback` *after* the chatbot has already emitted its final AI message with no tool call. So when the manifest is built and the answer text is generated, **the Auditor has not run yet** — `audit_results` doesn't exist. There is no way for that answer to correctly say "Auditor-verified evidence," "explicitly contradicted," etc., because those verdicts don't exist at generation time.
- **No post-audit synthesis step exists.** After `auditor`/`feedback` run, nothing recomposes or amends the answer using `claims`/`audit_results`. The `__main__` loop only re-prints the same unchanged AI message plus raw debug dumps of claims/audit_results/lessons — it never produces a corrected final answer reflecting audit verdicts.

So today: fetched vs. search-snippet mislabeling is *mitigated* (via prompting, before verification), but the core "auditor supported/contradicted" labeling requirement is structurally unreachable given current node ordering.

**4. Remaining issue**

The final user-facing answer is generated in `chatbot()` before `extract_claims`/`auditor`/`feedback` execute, so it can never truthfully reflect `audited_supported`/`audited_contradicted`/`failed` verdicts, and even the fetched/unfetched labeling it does attempt is prompt-compliance-based rather than deterministically constructed from state.

Add a deterministic final-answer composition step that runs **after** `auditor`/`feedback` (a new graph node, e.g. `compose_final_answer`, inserted between `feedback` and `END`), which builds the evidence labeling by **Python code reading `state["claims"]` and `state["audit_results"]`**, not by LLM prompt compliance — mapping each claim's `verification_status` directly to its required label:

- `failed` → "explicitly unverified/unsupported"

This becomes (or appends to) the actual text shown to the user, replacing reliance on the pre-audit `chatbot()` message as the final answer. The existing `analyze_tool_history`/manifest work in `chatbot()` can stay as a soft guardrail for the LLM's *drafting* pass, but it cannot be the source of truth for the labels — the new deterministic step must be.

The implementation is done and tested. Here's the report:

## Report

**1. Files changed**
- `app/main.py` only (per instruction #12/#14). No other files touched. The scratchpad test script (`test_compose_final_answer.py`) lives outside the repo.

**2. Exact graph flow**
```
START → chatbot ⇄ tools → extract_claims → auditor → feedback → compose_final_answer → END
```
Verified structurally by introspecting the compiled graph — `compose_final_answer` is the last node before `__end__`.

**3. How final evidence labels are determined**
- New module-level dict `EVIDENCE_STATUS_LABELS` + `get_evidence_label(verification_status)` (`app/main.py:227-240`) is the single source of truth — pure Python, no LLM involved.
- New node `compose_final_answer` (`app/main.py:525-591`) runs after `feedback`, reads `state["claims"]` and `state["audit_results"]`, joins them by `(original_claim, source_url)` — so each URL keeps its own independent status, never merged — and builds the final answer text entirely in Python from `verification_status`. No LLM call happens in this node at all (satisfies #9's stricter option: zero risk of the model inventing labels).
- `analyze_tool_history`'s manifest in `chatbot()` is untouched and still runs, but it only shapes the pre-audit *draft* the LLM produces for `extract_claims` to read — that draft is no longer shown to the user.
- CLI loop (`app/main.py:~665-688`) no longer prints the chatbot's draft AI content; it only prints tool-call activity during the loop, then prints `event["messages"][-1]` (the `compose_final_answer` output) once as `"Agent (Verified Final Answer):"` after the stream ends.

**4. Test results**
No existing test suite existed in the repo, so I wrote a synthetic regression test (no live API calls — fast, deterministic, zero cost) exercising `compose_final_answer` and `get_evidence_label` directly against hand-built structured state:

```
OK: unverified -> Search Snippets
OK: fetched -> Fetched Page Content
OK: audited_supported -> Auditor-verified evidence
OK: audited_contradicted -> contradicted wording
OK: failed -> explicitly unverified wording
OK: failed label never claims 'fetched'
... (403 case, supported case, contradicted case, multi-URL case)
ALL CHECKS PASSED (21/21)
```
`python -c "import ast; ast.parse(...)"` confirms the file parses; `app.main` imports cleanly and the compiled graph structure matches expectations.

I did not run a live end-to-end query through the real LLM/Tavily/fetch pipeline — that would spend real API quota and wasn't necessary to validate the fix, since the bug and the fix are entirely in `compose_final_answer`'s deterministic logic, not in the Analyst/Auditor prompts (which are unchanged).

**5. Does the 403 regression now pass?**
Yes. Synthetic 403 scenario (Microsoft/OpenAI ownership claim, `verification_status="failed"`) produces: *"Unverified - source could not be independently fetched or verified"* — and explicitly asserts neither "Fetched Page Content" nor "Auditor-verified evidence (SUPPORTED)" appear anywhere in that claim's output.

**6. Do supported/contradicted cases reach the final answer correctly?**
Yes. `audited_supported` → *"Auditor-verified evidence (SUPPORTED)"* with the auditor's verdict/reasoning/excerpt surfaced. `audited_contradicted` → *"Auditor-verified evidence (CONTRADICTED by the cited source)"*, with the contradicting fact (2014 vs. the original 2010 claim) surfaced, while `original_claim` text remains unmodified — directly proving the Auditor's verdict now reaches the user-facing answer, and confirming Decision 3 (never rewrite the original claim) still holds.

No graph redesign, no changes to Auditor/Feedback logic, no new dependencies, no unrelated files touched.

## Benchmark Specification (Design Only — Nothing Implemented)

---

### 1. Proposed 8 Questions

All questions live in one connected domain (Microsoft / OpenAI / GitHub / Alphabet) so entities can be legitimately reused and chained, and so the adversarial final question can be built by subtly corrupting an earlier verified fact.

| # | Question | Category (required skill) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | In what month and year did Satya Nadella become CEO of Microsoft? | Basic factual research |
| 2 | What was Microsoft's total revenue for fiscal year 2024, according to its official financial filings? | Multi-source research |
| 3 | How much did Microsoft invest in OpenAI, and in which year(s) did those investments occur? | Entity reuse |
| 4 | How does Microsoft's fiscal year 2024 revenue compare to Alphabet's (Google's) fiscal year 2024 revenue — which company reported higher revenue? | Comparison |
| 5 | Did Microsoft lay off exactly 10,000 employees in January 2023? | Conflicting sources |
| 6 | Who is the current CEO of the company that owns GitHub, and in what year did that company acquire GitHub? | Multi-hop research |
| 7 | Was Elon Musk a co-founder of OpenAI, and did he leave OpenAI's board in 2018? | Difficult source verification |
| 8 | Confirm: In 2019, Microsoft fully acquired OpenAI for $1 billion, making OpenAI a wholly-owned Microsoft subsidiary. | Adversarial / challenging final question |

---

### 2. Difficulty Progression

| # | Difficulty | Research objective | Expected complexity | Why it's harder than the previous question |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1/8 | Verify one well-documented date from an authoritative source rather than trusting the popular (and previously buggy — see DECISIONS.md's "Satya Nadella 2010 bug") date. | 1 search, 1 fetch, 1 claim. | Baseline. |
| 2 | 2/8 | Cross-check a numeric figure across ≥2 independently fetched sources (investor relations page + a secondary financial source), since "revenue" can be reported differently. | 2+ searches, 2+ fetches. | A single fact vs. a number that must be reconciled across multiple independently fetched sources. |
| 3 | 3/8 | Explicitly reuses "Microsoft" while introducing "OpenAI," and decomposes into a multi-year investment timeline (2019/2021/2023 tranches) instead of one static fact. | Multiple claims, each needing its own source/status. | Single question now yields multiple sub-claims, testing that per-claim status isn't merged. |
| 4 | 4/8 | Fetch and verify two companies' figures, then perform a comparative judgment. | ≥2 independently fetched primary sources + 1 derived comparison claim. | Introduces a second full research subject (Alphabet) plus a synthesized claim with no single source of its own. |
| 5 | 5/8 | Surface disagreement in reported layoff figures/dates rather than silently picking one source. | Multiple conflicting search results; verdict must reflect the discrepancy. | Sources now actively disagree (not just reinforce), forcing explicit contradiction/partial-support handling. |
| 6 | 6/8 | Two-step chain: who owns GitHub → that owner's current CEO + acquisition year, each hop independently verified. | ≥2 chained claims, each with its own source/status. | A dependency chain across multiple facts, not just conflicting numbers on one fact. |
| 7 | 7/8 | Verify a commonly oversimplified narrative (Musk "co-founder," 2018 board departure) against precise sourcing rather than a near-match snippet. | Sources vary in precision; tests the "unsupported/insufficient evidence" path. | Truth depends on nuance most sources state imprecisely — the system must resist declaring "supported" on a near-match. |
| 8 | 8/8 | Adversarial compound claim: correct facts ($1B, 2019) fused with a false framing ("fully acquired," "wholly-owned subsidiary"). Auditor must contradict the false part without accepting or rejecting the claim wholesale, and must not rewrite the original (false) claim. | Highest — partial contradiction of a compound claim. | Tests resistance to a plausible, engineered false claim — adversarial robustness, not just source ambiguity. |

---

### 3. Entity Reuse Plan

| Entity | Introduced in | Reused in |
|---|---|---|
| Microsoft | Q1 | Q2, Q3, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q8 |
| Satya Nadella | Q1 | Q6 |
| Fiscal Year 2024 | Q2 | Q4 |
| OpenAI | Q3 | Q7, Q8 |
| Alphabet / Google | Q4 | — |
| Jan 2023 layoffs | Q5 | — |
| GitHub | Q6 | — |
| Elon Musk | Q7 | — |

6 of 8 questions reuse at least one earlier entity (requirement was ≥2). Q8 deliberately introduces **no new entity** — it's a pure adversarial reuse of Q3's Microsoft/OpenAI/2019 investment fact, corrupted into a false "acquisition" framing.

---

### 4. Metric Schema

Per-question record (one JSON object per question per run):

```json
{
  "question_id": 1,
  "question": "string",
  "difficulty": 1,
  "category": "basic_factual",
  "timestamp": "ISO-8601, stamped by harness after run completes",

  "elapsed_seconds": 0.0,

  "tokens": {
    "input_tokens": 0,
    "output_tokens": 0,
    "total_tokens": 0
  },
  "cost_inr": {
    "llm_cost_inr": null,
    "search_cost_inr": null,
    "total_cost_inr": null,
    "note": "null until pricing config is supplied (see Open Config Items below)"
  },

  "tool_usage": {
    "num_searches": 0,
    "num_page_fetches": 0,
    "successful_fetches": 0,
    "failed_fetches": 0
  },

  "claims": {
    "num_claims": 0,
    "supported": 0,
    "contradicted": 0,
    "unsupported": 0
  },

  "feedback": {
    "lessons_generated": 0,
    "new_lessons_added_to_memory": 0,
    "memory_lessons_available_at_start": 0
  },

  "final_answer_excerpt": "string, truncated"
}
```

Derivation source for each metric (no `main.py` change required for most of these — computed post-hoc from final graph state):

| Metric | Derived from |
|---|---|
| `elapsed_seconds` | Harness-level wall clock around the graph invocation. |
| `input/output/total_tokens` | LangChain `UsageMetadataCallbackHandler` attached at invocation time (see Open Design Question below) — aggregates usage across chatbot, extract_claims, auditor, and feedback LLM calls. |
| `cost_inr.*` | `tokens × price-per-token config` — **left null** until pricing is supplied. |
| `num_searches` / `num_page_fetches` | Count of `tool` messages in `state["messages"]` by originating tool name. |
| `successful_fetches` / `failed_fetches` | Count of `[FETCH STATUS: SUCCESS]` vs `[FETCH STATUS: FAILED]` markers in fetch tool messages (same parsing convention `analyze_tool_history` already uses). |
| `num_claims` / `supported` / `contradicted` / `unsupported` | `state["claims"]` (`verification_status`) and `state["audit_results"]` (`verdict`). |
| `lessons_generated` | `len(state["feedback_lessons"])` returned by `feedback()`... actually `feedback_lessons` in state is already just the *added* (non-duplicate) set — harness will also capture the LLM's raw `new_lessons` count for "generated vs added" distinction if needed. |
| `new_lessons_added_to_memory` | Diff of `research_memory.json` line count before vs. after the question run. |
| `memory_lessons_available_at_start` | `len(load_memory())` snapshotted **before** the question runs (memory only grows at the very end via `feedback()`, so this is stable for the whole run). |

**Self-improvement signal:** benchmark run should track `memory_lessons_available_at_start` per question across a full 8-question pass, and ideally re-run the same 8 questions in a second pass to see if `supported`-claim rate goes up / `unsupported` rate goes down as memory accumulates lessons.

**Open config items (not invented, need to be supplied before cost numbers are real):**
- `GEMINI_INPUT_COST_PER_1K_TOKENS_INR`, `GEMINI_OUTPUT_COST_PER_1K_TOKENS_INR` (model is `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` per `app/main.py:210`)
- `TAVILY_COST_PER_SEARCH_INR`
- USD→INR conversion rate/date, if pricing is only available in USD

### 5. Files Recommended (for after approval — none created yet)

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `benchmark/questions.json` | The 8 structured question definitions (question, difficulty, objective, entities_introduced, entities_reused, expected_complexity, difficulty_delta). |
| `benchmark/run_benchmark.py` | Harness: iterates questions, snapshots memory before/after, times execution, attaches a usage-metadata callback, invokes `agent` from `app/main.py` unmodified, parses final state into the metric schema above, writes results. |
| `benchmark/results/` | Output directory — one timestamped JSON (and optionally CSV) per run. |
| `benchmark/pricing_config.json` (or `.env` additions) | Placeholder for the INR pricing config listed above — ships with `null`/TODO values, not invented numbers. |
| `benchmark/BENCHMARK_SPEC.md` | This specification, committed for the record (same convention as STATUS/HANDOFF/DECISIONS). |

**Open design question to flag before implementation:** `extract_claims`, `auditor`, and `feedback` each call `llm.invoke(...)` / `structured_llm.invoke(...)` directly and don't currently return those calls into `state["messages"]`, so token usage for those calls isn't visible in graph state today. My plan is to capture it via LangChain's `UsageMetadataCallbackHandler` passed through `agent.invoke(..., config={"callbacks": [...]})`, relying on LangChain's contextvar-based callback propagation to nested synchronous `invoke()` calls inside node functions — this requires **zero changes to `app/main.py`**, but I haven't verified propagation actually reaches those nested calls in this LangGraph version. I'll validate that narrowly during implementation and fall back to a minimal non-architectural instrumentation shim only if propagation doesn't work — will flag it before touching anything if so.

\"cost_status\": \"computed\",\n    }\n\n\ndef run_question(question: dict, pricing: dict) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Runs exactly one question through the real, unmodified agent and\n    returns its metric }

71	### Derivation
72	
73	| Metric | Source |
74	|---|---|
75	| `elapsed_seconds` | Harness wall-clock around `agent.invoke()` for that question. |
76	| `input_tokens` / `output_tokens` / `total_tokens` | `langchain_core.callbacks.UsageMetadataCallbackHandler` attached at the top-level `agent.invoke(..., config={"callbacks": [handler]})` call. Confirmed (see "Nested Token Tracking Validation" below) to capture usage from LLM calls made inside `chatbot`, `extract_claims`, `auditor`, and `feedback` even though none of those node functions accept or forward an explicit `config` parameter - LangChain/LangGraph propagate the callback via a contextvar automatically. **No `app/main.py` changes were required.** |
77	| `*_cost_inr` | `tokens * price` from `pricing_config.json`. Null until real pricing is supplied - see that file. |
78	| `num_searches` / `num_page_fetches` | Count of `tool`-type messages in the final state's `messages` list, grouped by originating tool name (`web_search` vs `fetch_page`). |
79	| `successful_fetches` / `failed_fetches` | Count of `[FETCH STATUS: SUCCESS]` / `[FETCH STATUS: FAILED]` markers within `fetch_page` tool messages - same convention `analyze_tool_history()` in `app/main.py` already uses. |
80	| `num_claims` / `supported_claims` / `contradicted_claims` / `unsupported_claims` | `state["claims"]` (`verification_status`) cross-referenced with `state["audit_results"]` (`verdict`). |
81	| `lessons_generated` | Length of `feedback_lessons` returned in final state (already deduplicated against existing memory by `add_lessons_to_memory`). |
82	| `new_lessons_added_to_memory` | Diff of `app/research_memory.json` entry count, snapshotted before vs. after the question. |
83	| `memory_lessons_available_at_start` | Length of the pre-question memory snapshot (this is what was actually available to `chatbot()`'s system prompt for this question, since memory only grows via `feedback()` at the very end of a question's graph run). |
84	| `final_answer_excerpt` | First ~500 characters of `compose_final_answer`'s output message (the last message in final state). |

Success/failure is derived from `audit_results[].supporting_evidence`: on a real fetch failure, `auditor()` sets `supporting_evidence` to the raw fetched-page string, which starts with the literal `[FETCH STATUS: FAILED]` marker; on any fetch success (regardless of whether the resulting verdict is supported, contradicted, or unsupported-due-to-insufficient-evidence, and even if the post-fetch audit judgement itself errored) `supporting_evidence` holds an LLM-extracted quote or error text with no such marker. `verification_status == \"failed\"` is *not* a reliable signal by itself, since it's also used for the succeeded-fetch-but-inconclusive-judgement cases - see `count_auditor_fetches()` in `run_benchmark.py` and its fixture test in `test_count_auditor_fetches.py`. |\n| `num_claims` / `supported_claims` / `contradicted_claims` / `unsupported_claims` | `state[\"claims\"]` (`verification_status`) cross-referenced with `state[\"audit_results\"]` (`verdict`). |"

## 3. QUESTION-BY-QUESTION COMPARISON

**Q1 — Basic factual (Satya Nadella CEO date)**
- Pass 1: 10.84s, 12,752 tok, 1 search, 1 auditor fetch (success), SUPPORTED, 0 lessons
- Pass 2: 11.58s, 13,983 tok, 1 search, 1 auditor fetch (success), SUPPORTED, 0 lessons
- Change: essentially flat (±1s, ±1.2k tokens)
- Interpretation: **Inconclusive.** Identical outcome and shape; too small a delta to attribute to anything.

**Q2 — Multi-source (MS FY2024 revenue)**
- Pass 1: 12.32s, 16,584 tok, SUPPORTED
- Pass 2: **254.81s**, 17,576 tok, SUPPORTED (same source URL both times: microsoft.com/investor/reports/ar24)
- Change: outcome identical; elapsed time ballooned 20x
- Interpretation: **Inconclusive** on learning. The log shows no retry/error/rate-limit messages around this call — token count is nearly identical to Pass 1, so this wasn't extra work, just latency (external API/network variance). This is noise, not a behavioral signal, and should not be read either way.

**Q3 — Entity reuse (MS→OpenAI investment)**
- Pass 1: 12.56s, 13,061 tok, SUPPORTED (source: cnbc.com)
- Pass 2: 13.70s, 14,786 tok, SUPPORTED (same cnbc.com source)
- Change: flat, same source reused
- Interpretation: **Inconclusive.** Same outcome, same source, negligible deltas.

**Q4 — Comparison (MS vs Alphabet FY2024 revenue)** — the one question with a real behavioral shift
- Pass 1: 14.08s→51.59s (varied by run), 1 combined claim, 1 auditor fetch (failed on SEC/last10k), UNSUPPORTED, 1 lesson
- Pass 2: 25.43s, **2 separate claims**, 2 auditor fetches (1 success on microsoft.com, 1 failed on macrotrends.net), **both claims UNSUPPORTED**, 4x the tokens (84,546 vs ~39-40k), 4 searches vs 2-3
- Change: Analyst extraction changed from 1 merged comparison claim → 2 separately-sourced claims (one per company) — this is exactly the behavior a Pass-1 lesson ("ensure all comparative entities... individually retrieved and verified") should produce.
- Interpretation: **Some evidence of learning, but it backfired this run.** The lesson plausibly changed *how* the Analyst decomposed the question (splitting entities for independent verification, which is the correct instinct). But it cost far more tokens/searches, and one of the two independent fetches still failed, so the final answer is still fully unsupported — no net quality gain, and a real cost regression. This is the clearest trace of memory actually altering behavior in Pass 2, but the outcome is not better.

**Q5 — Conflicting sources (MS Jan 2023 layoffs)**
- Pass 1: 26.79s, 14,157 tok, SUPPORTED (blogs.microsoft.com)
- Pass 2: 29.56s, 13,995 tok, SUPPORTED (same blogs.microsoft.com source)
- Change: flat
- Interpretation: **Inconclusive.** Same source, same outcome both passes.

**Q6 — Multi-hop (GitHub owner → CEO → acquisition year)**
- Pass 1: 13.24s, 14,109 tok, SUPPORTED (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GitHub)
- Pass 2: **614.18s**, 14,826 tok, SUPPORTED (same Wikipedia source)
- Change: outcome identical; elapsed time ballooned ~46x
- Interpretation: **Inconclusive** on learning, same reasoning as Q2 — token count is flat, no errors logged, this is latency noise from the live API, not a behavioral change. Worth flagging operationally (a >10-minute single-question latency is a real reliability concern for future runs) but not evidence of learning either direction.

**Q7 — Difficult source verification (Musk/OpenAI)**
- Pass 1: 12.99s, 14,356 tok, SUPPORTED (fortune.com)
- Pass 2: 11.60s, 12,826 tok, SUPPORTED (same fortune.com source)
- Change: flat, slightly fewer tokens
- Interpretation: **Inconclusive.** Same source, same outcome, small delta not attributable to anything specific.

**Q8 — Adversarial (false MS "acquired" OpenAI claim)** — the question you flagged to watch closely
- Pass 1: 15.93s, 15,310 tok, source: `unanswered.io/guide/is-tableau-owned-by-salesforce` (**topically unrelated** to the claim), auditor fetch **succeeded**, verdict **CONTRADICTED**
- Pass 2: 9.44s, 12,162 tok, source: `reuters.com/article/technology/microsoft-to-invest-1-billion-in-openai-...` (**highly relevant, correct source**), auditor fetch **FAILED**, verdict **UNSUPPORTED**
- Change: source selection quality clearly improved (Reuters article about the actual 2019 $1B investment is exactly the right source, vs. an unrelated Tableau/Salesforce page). But the fetch itself failed this time, so the final answer only says "could not be independently verified" rather than actively contradicting the false "fully acquired... wholly-owned subsidiary" framing.
- Interpretation: **Mixed — some evidence of improved source selection, but a regression in the final verdict's usefulness.** Better source targeting is a plausible effect of accumulated lessons (several memory lessons specifically address "verify acquisition/ownership claims against primary news," added after Q8 in Pass 1). But because the correct source failed to fetch, Pass 2's final answer is *weaker* for the exact adversarial case you asked me to watch: it no longer actively flags the false claim as contradicted, just as unverifiable. A user reading only the Pass 2 answer would not learn the claim is false.

## 4. DID THE SYSTEM SHOW EVIDENCE OF LEARNING?

**Overall: Inconclusive, with one instance of Some Evidence (Q4) and one Mixed/partial-regression case (Q8).**

- **No question shows Strong evidence.** Nothing here is a clean, unambiguous case of higher-quality output at lower cost.
- **Some evidence (Q4):** memory lessons plausibly changed the Analyst's claim-decomposition strategy (splitting a comparison into per-entity claims) — a real behavioral shift traceable to a specific prior lesson. But it didn't improve the outcome (still unsupported) and cost 4x the tokens.
- **Mixed (Q8):** source selection got measurably better and more topically relevant, consistent with the ownership/acquisition-verification lessons added after Pass 1's Q8. But the overall verdict quality regressed (contradicted → unsupported) due to an unrelated fetch failure, not due to worse reasoning.
- **5 of 8 questions (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q5, Q7) are flat-to-inconclusive** — same source, same verdict, same claim count both passes. No detectable memory effect.
- **Aggregate numbers (more tokens, more searches, more unsupported claims, fewer contradicted, much higher total time) look worse in Pass 2**, but this is dominated by: (a) two outlier latency spikes (Q2, Q6) that are almost certainly external API/network noise, not system behavior, and (b) live search returning different, sometimes-less-reliable source URLs between runs (nondeterminism), which is exactly the confound you warned against over-interpreting.

Per your instruction, I'm not calling any of this "improvement" or "regression" in the strong sense — the honest read is **the two live runs are too noisy and too small (n=8, single trial per pass) to separate a real memory effect from search/API nondeterminism**, except for Q4's claim-decomposition change, which is a real, attributable behavioral shift with a neutral-to-negative outcome.

## 5. WHAT STILL NEEDS TO BE FIXED?

1. **Q8 (adversarial) verdict is fetch-failure-fragile.** Whether the false claim gets correctly labeled CONTRADICTED depends entirely on whether the Auditor's one fetch attempt happens to succeed. There's no fallback (e.g., trying a second source) when the single cited URL fails — this is a real gap for exactly the adversarial case this benchmark is meant to stress-test. (Not proposing a fix yet, per your instructions — just naming it.)
2. **Pass 1's Q8 "CONTRADICTED" was itself questionable**: it was driven by a fetched page that was topically unrelated to the claim (Tableau/Salesforce), not a genuine refutation. So neither pass actually produced a *rigorously sourced* contradiction for Q8 — Pass 1 got the right label for the wrong reason, Pass 2 got a defensible label (unsupported) for the right reason (fetch failed) but weaker practical output.
3. **Two extreme latency outliers (254s and 614s)** with no logged cause — worth instrumenting (e.g., capturing per-LLM-call and per-tool-call timing, not just total elapsed_seconds) before drawing any timing conclusions in future passes.
4. **Single-fetch-source fragility in general**: every question in both passes relied on exactly one cited source with no retry/fallback if that fetch fails (Q4 in both passes, Q8 in Pass 2) — this is a structural limitation of the current Auditor, not a benchmark issue.
5. **n=1 per pass is too small** to distinguish "did the system learn" from "did search return different sources this time." A real answer needs either multiple repetitions per pass or a controlled way to hold search results fixed.

## 6. RECOMMENDED NEXT IMPLEMENTATION STEP

Given the above, the highest-value next step is **not** a memory/prompt change yet — it's tightening the benchmark's own measurement rigor so a future Pass 3 (after any real fix) produces an interpretable signal:
- Capture per-call latency breakdown (search vs. fetch vs. each LLM call) instead of only total `elapsed_seconds`, so latency spikes like Q2/Q6 can be diagnosed rather than guessed at.
- Consider running each question N≥3 times per pass (or at least re-running Pass 2 once more) before concluding anything about learning, since single-trial live-search results are too noisy on their own.

That's a benchmark-only change, consistent with "no architecture changes yet." I have not implemented anything — this is the analysis for you to decide what to do next.

74	### Derivation
75	
76	| Metric | Source |
77	|---|---|
78	| `elapsed_seconds` | Harness wall-clock around `agent.invoke()` for that question. |
79	| `input_tokens` / `output_tokens` / `total_tokens` | `langchain_core.callbacks.UsageMetadataCallbackHandler` attached at the top-level `agent.invoke(..., config={"callbacks": [handler]})` call. Confirmed (see "Nested Token Tracking Validation" below) to capture usage from LLM calls made inside `chatbot`, `extract_claims`, `auditor`, and `feedback` even though none of those node functions accept or forward an explicit `config` parameter - LangChain/LangGraph propagate the callback via a contextvar automatically. **No `app/main.py` changes were required.** |
80	| `*_cost_inr` | `tokens * price` from `pricing_config.json`. Null until real pricing is supplied - see that file. |
81	| `num_searches` / `num_page_fetches` | Count of `tool`-type messages in the final state's `messages` list, grouped by originating tool name (`web_search` vs `fetch_page`). **These are Analyst-initiated fetches only** - see next row for the separate Auditor-initiated fetch count. |
82	| `successful_fetches` / `failed_fetches` | Count of `[FETCH STATUS: SUCCESS]` / `[FETCH STATUS: FAILED]` markers within `fetch_page` tool messages - same convention `analyze_tool_history()` in `app/main.py` already uses. Also Analyst-initiated only. |
83	| `auditor_fetches` / `auditor_successful_fetches` / `auditor_failed_fetches` | The Auditor's own independent verification fetches, tracked **separately** from the Analyst's fetches above since these are what actually drive each claim's verdict. `auditor()` calls `fetch_page.invoke()` directly (not through the `tools` node, so it never appears in `state["messages"]`) - once per claim, always - so `len(audit_results) == auditor_fetches`. Success/failure is derived from `audit_results[].supporting_evidence`: on a real fetch failure, `auditor()` sets `supporting_evidence` to the raw fetched-page string, which starts with the literal `[FETCH STATUS: FAILED]` marker; on any fetch success (regardless of whether the resulting verdict is supported, contradicted, or unsupported-due-to-insufficient-evidence, and even if the post-fetch audit judgement itself errored) `supporting_evidence` holds an LLM-extracted quote or error text with no such marker. `verification_status == "failed"` is *not* a reliable signal by itself, since it's also used for the succeeded-fetch-but-inconclusive-judgement cases - see `count_auditor_fetches()` in `run_benchmark.py` and its fixture test in `test_count_auditor_fetches.py`. |
84	| `num_claims` / `supported_claims` / `contradicted_claims` / `unsupported_claims` | `state["claims"]` (`verification_status`) cross-referenced with `state["audit_results"]` (`verdict`). |
85	| `lessons_generated` | Length of `feedback_lessons` returned in final state (already deduplicated against existing memory by `add_lessons_to_memory`). |
86	| `new_lessons_added_to_memory` | Diff of `app/research_memory.json` entry count, snapshotted before vs. after the question. |
87	| `memory_lessons_available_at_start` | Length of the pre-question memory snapshot (this is what was actually available to `chatbot()`'s system prompt for this question, since memory only grows via `feedback()` at the very end of a question's graph run). |
88	| `final_answer_excerpt` | First ~500 characters of `compose_final_answer`'s output message (the last message in final state). |

## Report

### 1. Files changed

- `benchmark/run_benchmark.py` — added:
  - `TimingCallbackHandler(BaseCallbackHandler)`: attributes every LLM call and every tool call to the graph node it happened in, using only standard LangChain callback events (`on_chain_start/end`, `on_chat_model_start`, `on_llm_end/error`, `on_tool_start`, `on_tool_end/error`) — no `app/main.py` changes.
  - `summarize_timing(records)`: aggregates raw records into the requested breakdown.
  - Wired both into `run_question()` (added alongside the existing `UsageMetadataCallbackHandler` in the same `config={"callbacks": [...]}` call) and added `timing_summary`/`timing_log` to the result dict; added `None`/`[]` equivalents to `run_question_safe`'s failure record.
  - Extended the per-question console log line with an `llm(...)/search=.../fetch=.../unaccounted=...` breakdown.
- `benchmark/BENCHMARK_SPEC.md` — documented the two new fields, the caveat about `success` meaning "didn't raise" vs. semantic fetch success, and the validation work.
- `benchmark/test_timing_instrumentation.py` (new) — 25-check fixture test, zero API cost.

**Not touched:** `app/main.py`, Analyst/Auditor/Feedback/memory logic, `benchmark/questions.json`, `benchmark/pricing_config.json`, and all four existing result files (verified via unchanged mtimes above).

### 2. What timing data is captured

Per question, added (alongside all existing metrics, unchanged):

- `timing_log`: raw list of records, each `{question_id, pass_id, operation_type, node, detail, start_offset_seconds, elapsed_seconds, success, error}`.
- `timing_summary`: aggregated —
  - `llm_chatbot_seconds` / `llm_extract_claims_seconds` / `llm_auditor_seconds` / `llm_feedback_seconds` / `llm_unknown_seconds` (+ `llm_total_seconds`)
  - `search_seconds`, `fetch_seconds`, `other_tool_seconds` (+ `tool_total_seconds`)
  - `timed_total_seconds` (llm + tool)
  - `num_llm_calls`, `num_search_calls`, `num_fetch_calls`, `num_failed_calls`
  - `node_total_seconds` per graph node + `node_sum_seconds`
  - `unaccounted_seconds` = question `elapsed_seconds` − `node_sum_seconds` — this is the key diagnostic for the Q2/Q6 outliers: a large value means the delay isn't explained by any captured LLM/tool call at all (e.g. a hidden SDK-level retry or network wait), a small value with one dominant `llm_*`/`search`/`fetch` bucket means we can point at exactly which call was slow.

Attribution correctly distinguishes Analyst-routed tool calls (via the real `ToolNode`, node=`"tools"`) from Auditor's direct `fetch_page.invoke()` calls (node=`"auditor"`), and correctly resolves through `with_structured_output`'s extra `RunnableSequence` wrapper layer (validated against the real Gemini API before implementation, then covered by the fixture test with a fake model).

### 3. Existing benchmark behavior: unchanged

- All previously-existing metrics/fields are untouched — only new fields (`timing_summary`, `timing_log`) were added.
- `--dry-run` still passes.
- `test_count_auditor_fetches.py` (prior fixture test) still passes unmodified — confirms the earlier auditor-fetch logic wasn't disturbed.
- No live questions were run — no tokens/searches/fetches spent, no memory mutation, no new results file written.

- `test_timing_instrumentation.py`: 25/25 — covers node attribution (chatbot/tools/extract_claims/auditor/feedback), ToolNode vs. direct-invoke tool paths, success/failure flagging including a simulated exception, `question_id`/`pass_id` stamping, and aggregation-math correctness in `summarize_timing`.

# Persistent Research Memory — Architecture Review

Scope inspected: `app/research_memory.json` (28 lessons), the memory mechanism in `app/main.py` (`load_memory` / `add_lessons_to_memory` / injection in the `chatbot` node), and the Pass 1/2/3 result files. Grounding measurements were computed read-only.

## 1. The 28 lessons, grouped

Numbering in file order. Every lesson has `source_of_feedback: "auditor"`.

**Category A — "Fetch the full page instead of trusting the search snippet" (~13 lessons):** #2, #8, #9, #10, #12, #16, #17, #20, #21, #23, #24, #26, #27
The single largest group. All say essentially the same thing (retrieve the full page before asserting a fact) specialized to a topic: dates/appointments (#8, #23), revenue (#9), investment timelines (#10, #24), layoffs (#12, #20, #26), subsidiary/parent leadership (#16, #21, #27), board departures (#17).

**Category B — HTTP-error handling / avoid inaccessible URLs / seek alternatives (~11 lessons):** #1, #2, #4, #5, #6, #7, #11, #13, #15, #25, #28
Mostly about 403 (especially SEC EDGAR), plus 404 (#13) and 401 (#28). Advice: prefer fetchable sources, fall back to investor-relations portals / open aggregators / mirrors.

**Category C — Distinguish minority investment vs. full acquisition (3 lessons):** #14, #18, #22
All three are the Q8 lesson (don't mischaracterize the MS/OpenAI partnership as an acquisition).

**Category D — Verify comparative/multi-entity claims per entity (1–2 lessons):** #19 (clean), #27 (straddles A/D — "fetch both parent and subsidiary pages").
This is the Q4/Q6 decomposition lesson.

**Category E — Verify specific figures/percentages against primary sources (1 lesson):** #3 (overlaps A).

## 2. Duplicates / near-duplicates

The dedup logic (`add_lessons_to_memory`) only blocks **exact normalized-string matches** (`strip().lower()`). The Feedback LLM paraphrases every pass, so paraphrases slip through. Near-duplicate clusters:

- **#12 ≈ #20 ≈ #26** — "always fetch the full corporate blog post/press release to verify exact employment reduction figures rather than relying on search snippets." #12 and #20 differ only by the word "the". Three copies of one idea.
- **#4 ≈ #5 ≈ #6 ≈ #15 ≈ #25** — "SEC EDGAR direct URLs 403; use investor-relations/alternative sources." Five variants of one idea.
- **#8 ≈ #23** — "fetch full page to verify exact historical dates/appointments." Near-identical.
- **#10 ≈ #24** — "fetch full page for multi-year investment timelines." Near-identical.
- **#14 ≈ #18 ≈ #22** — "distinguish minority investment from full acquisition." Three variants.
- **#16 ≈ #21** — "fetch full page for subsidiary/parent leadership." Near-identical.

**Conservatively, the 28 lessons express roughly 5–6 distinct ideas.** De-duplication would collapse them to about that many.

## 3. Lessons too specific to one benchmark question

Many lessons bake in a specific entity/domain that won't generalize:
- SEC-EDGAR-specific (#4, #5, #6, #15, #25) — names a specific site.
- MS/OpenAI-acquisition-specific (#14, #18, #22) — one claim.
- "Gurufocus URL" / "Satya Nadella's ownership percentage" (#7), "Alphabet's revenue" (#11), "Microsoft layoff" (#12, #20, #26) — question-bound phrasing.

These are effectively **memorized answers to benchmark questions**, not transferable research policy.

## 4. Genuinely reusable agent behavior

Distilled, the reusable core is small:
1. **Don't treat a search snippet as verified evidence — fetch the primary source** (Category A, E).
2. **When a source is inaccessible (4xx), fall back to an alternative accessible source rather than asserting or abandoning** (Category B).
3. **Verify each entity/sub-claim of a multi-part or comparative question independently** (Category D).
4. **Check the *nature* of a corporate relationship (investment vs. acquisition vs. subsidiary) against primary announcements before affirming it** (Category C, generalized to "verify claim *type*, not just figures").

That's it — 4 durable principles behind 28 rows.

## 5. Cost of injecting all 28 into every Analyst prompt

Measured against the exact injection format in `app/main.py`:

- **9,135 characters ≈ 2,284 tokens** per chatbot call.
- **Reasons are 50% of that body text** — and reasons are *audit justifications* ("the fetch failed with 403…"), not guidance the Analyst needs. Half the payload is arguably dead weight.
- The `chatbot` node runs ~2× per question, so ≈ **4,600 memory tokens/question**, ≈ **36k tokens/pass**, before any question content.
- On a light question (Q1, Pass 3: 12,974 input tokens total) memory is ~35% of input; on heavier questions it's a smaller share (swamped by search-result content).

**Assessment: not yet a crisis, but the trajectory is the problem.** It grows ~+4–6 lessons/pass with no cap and no real dedup, so it compounds. The per-question input-token signal is currently noisy (Q8 input tokens actually *fell* as memory grew, because search content dominates), so I won't claim a clean cost regression *yet* — but unbounded monotonic growth of a mostly-redundant block is a clear latent cost and context-dilution risk.

## 6. Conflicts between lessons

No hard "do X" / "never do X" contradictions, but two real tensions:

- **"Prefer primary/authoritative sources" (#3, #14, #22) vs. "avoid 403-prone primary sources like SEC EDGAR, use secondary aggregators" (#4–7, #15, #25).** The most authoritative sources (SEC filings) are exactly the ones that fail the Auditor's fetch. These pull the Analyst in opposite directions with no priority rule.
- **"Always fetch the full page even when the snippet already answered correctly."** Several Category-A lessons were generated on **successful** questions whose reasons explicitly say the snippet worked (#8, #23, #21). This nudges the Analyst toward extra fetches that add latency and *new failure surface* without adding correctness — a mild self-defeating pressure.

## 7. Individual lessons vs. compressed principles

The evidence points to **compression**. 28 rows encode ~5–6 ideas; the individual-lesson format is the *cause* of the bloat (each audit re-emits a paraphrase). Durable principles (a small, curated set) would preserve all the actual guidance at a fraction of the tokens and remove the conflicts by letting a principle state priority ("prefer primary sources; if inaccessible, fall back to a reputable secondary source and label accordingly").

## 8. Does memory actually influence observed behavior?

Critical mechanical finding first: **memory is injected ONLY into the `chatbot` (Analyst) node.** `extract_claims`, `auditor`, and `feedback` do **not** receive it (`feedback` loads memory only to avoid re-adding duplicates). This constrains what memory can and cannot cause.

- **Q8 source selection — plausible, direct, but unproven and outcome-neutral.** The chatbot picks sources and *does* see memory, so the acquisition-verification lessons (#14/#18/#22) *could* directly steer it. The source did shift from an unrelated page (Pass 1: `unanswered.io/…tableau…`) to a topically-correct one (Pass 2 & 3: the Reuters MS-invests-$1B-in-OpenAI article). That's **consistent with** memory influence. But it's confounded by live-search nondeterminism, and it **did not improve the verdict** — the Reuters fetch failed both times, yielding UNSUPPORTED (Pass 2, 3) instead of Pass 1's CONTRADICTED. Better-targeted source, worse usable answer.
- **Q4 claim decomposition — indirect at best, cannot be asserted causally.** Claim count is decided by `extract_claims`, which **never sees memory**. So lesson #19 cannot directly cause the 1→2 claim split. The only possible path is indirect: memory → chatbot gathers both entities' data → `extract_claims` then emits 2 claims. The split did appear (Pass 1: 1 claim; Pass 2 & 3: 2 claims) exactly after #19 entered memory at the end of Pass 1 — **consistent with** indirect influence, but confounded and unproven, and again outcome-neutral (both claims UNSUPPORTED in Pass 2 & 3).

**Bottom line for #8:** the mechanism *can* only plausibly move the Analyst node; the two candidate behavior changes are consistent-with memory influence but not demonstrably caused by it, and neither produced a better final verdict. There is **no benchmark evidence that memory has improved output quality** — only weak evidence it has changed behavior.

## 9. Recommended memory strategy (summary; detail in C)

Move from "append every auditor paraphrase, inject all verbatim" to **a small curated set of durable principles, deduplicated semantically, injected lesson-text-only (drop the reasons), with a size cap.**

---

# Deliverables

## A. Current memory assessment

A working, honest feedback loop that is **accumulating redundancy faster than knowledge**. 28 rows encode ~5–6 distinct ideas; ~50% of the injected payload is audit-justification text the Analyst doesn't need; growth is unbounded with no semantic dedup; and the guidance only reaches the Analyst node. It is functioning as designed but is architecturally on a path to context bloat and dilution, with no measured quality benefit so far.

## B. Problems

1. **Weak dedup** — exact-string only; the Feedback LLM's paraphrasing defeats it, so near-duplicates pile up (5 SEC-EDGAR variants, 3 acquisition variants, etc.).
2. **Redundancy** — ~5–6 ideas spread across 28 rows.
3. **Over-fitting to benchmark questions** — many lessons name specific sites/entities/claims; they're memorized answers, not policy.
4. **Reasons injected but not useful** — half the ~2,284-token payload is audit justification irrelevant to the Analyst.
5. **Unbounded growth** — no cap, no ranking, no relevance filtering; grows every pass.
6. **Internal tension** — "prefer primary sources" vs. "avoid 403-prone primary sources" with no priority; plus advice to always fetch even when the snippet was already correct.
7. **Limited reach** — injected only into `chatbot`; cannot directly influence `extract_claims`/`auditor`.
8. **No demonstrated quality lift** — behavior changes (Q4, Q8) are consistent-with but unproven, and outcome-neutral or worse.

## C. Recommended memory design

- **Curated principle set, not an append log.** Replace the growing list with a small set (target ~5–8) of durable, entity-agnostic principles covering: snippet-vs-fetch, 4xx fallback (with an explicit priority rule resolving the primary-vs-accessible tension), per-entity verification of multi-part claims, and claim-*type* verification (investment vs. acquisition).
- **Semantic dedup on write**, not exact-string — before adding, check similarity against existing principles (embedding or an LLM "is this already covered?" check) and merge rather than append.
- **Inject lesson text only; drop `reason`** from the Analyst prompt (keep reasons in the file for provenance/audit). ~50% token cut immediately.
- **Hard cap + relevance** — cap the injected set (e.g. top-N), and once curated it stays small by construction.
- **Keep entity-specific facts out of memory** — memory should hold *how to research*, never *the answer to a specific benchmark question*.

## D. Minimal implementation plan (for later — not now)

1. **One-time curation**: collapse the current 28 → ~5–8 principles (can be a scripted LLM pass over the file, reviewed by hand), written back to `research_memory.json` in the same schema.
2. **Injection change** (`chatbot` node): format lessons as lesson-text-only, and cap at N.
3. **Write-path change** (`add_lessons_to_memory`): add a semantic "already covered?" gate before append; on match, skip or merge instead of adding a paraphrase.
4. **Optional cap/pruning**: enforce a max size (e.g. keep the most general principles).
5. **Validate**: existing benchmark harness + a small fixture test for the new dedup/cap logic; then a Pass 4 to compare token cost and behavior against Pass 3.

All of that touches `app/main.py`'s memory functions and the file — **out of scope for this review**, listed only so the path is clear.

## E. Auditor fallback: before or after memory changes?

**Do the Auditor fallback FIRST, before the memory rework.** The benchmark shows the binding constraint on *answer quality* is not memory — it's that the Auditor makes a single fetch attempt with no fallback, so the correct source failing (Q4 both passes, Q8 in Pass 2 & 3) collapses a good answer to UNSUPPORTED. Memory changes, by the evidence here, are a **cost/scaling/hygiene** improvement with no demonstrated quality lift; the Auditor fallback is a **correctness** improvement that directly addresses the repeated failure mode. Sequencing rationale:

- Fixing the Auditor first removes the fetch-failure confound that currently masks whether *any* memory/source-selection change actually helps — after fallback, a Pass will show real verdict differences instead of everything bottlenecking on a failed fetch.
- Memory is not near a hard limit yet (~2,284 tokens/injection, noisy per-question cost), so deferring it one step costs little.

So: **Auditor fallback → re-benchmark → then memory curation/dedup**, measuring each independently.

101	def count_auditor_fetches(audit_results):
102	    """Derives Auditor-side fetch success/failure from audit_results, separately
103	    from the Analyst's own tool-call fetches (see count_tool_usage above).
104	
105	    app/main.py's auditor() always attempts exactly one independent fetch_page
106	    call per claim (or synthesizes a FAILED marker if there's no source_url),
107	    so len(audit_results) == number of Auditor fetch attempts.
108	
109	    On fetch failure, auditor() sets supporting_evidence to the raw fetched_data
110	    string, which starts with the literal "[FETCH STATUS: FAILED]" marker - so
111	    that marker's presence reliably identifies an Auditor fetch failure.
112	
113	    On fetch success, supporting_evidence instead holds an LLM-extracted quote
114	    (no fetch-status marker at all) - this is true whether the resulting verdict
115	    is supported, contradicted, OR unsupported-due-to-insufficient-evidence, and
116	    also true if the post-fetch audit judgement itself errored/returned empty.
117	    verification_status alone is NOT a reliable signal here, since "failed" is
118	    also used for those succeeded-fetch-but-inconclusive-judgement cases - only
119	    the literal marker in supporting_evidence distinguishes a real fetch failure.
120	    """
121	    auditor_fetches = len(audit_results)
122	    auditor_failed_fetches = sum(
123	        1 for a in audit_results
124	        if str(a.get("supporting_evidence", "")).startswith("[FETCH STATUS: FAILED]")
125	    )
126	    auditor_successful_fetches = auditor_fetches - auditor_failed_fetches
127	    return {
128	        "auditor_fetches": auditor_fetches,
129	        "auditor_successful_fetches": auditor_successful_fetches,
130	        "auditor_failed_fetches": auditor_failed_fetches,
