_build_fallback_query\nwith only app.main.llm.with_structured_output patched, to assert the prompt-level\nguards (requirement #6 \"unrelated -> not contradicted\", and the neutral fallback\nquery independence rule) without hitting the network.\n\nRun with:\n    python benchmark/test_auditor_fallback.py\n\"\"\"\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nREPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))\nsys.path.insert(0, REPO_ROOT)\n\nimport app.main as m\nfrom langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage\n\nfailures = []\n\n\ndef check(condition, message):\n    if not condition:\n        failures.append(message)\n        print(f\"FAIL: {message}\")\n    else:\n        print(f\"OK:   {message}\")\n\n\n# --- Fakes ---------------------------------------------------------------\n\nclass FakeTool:\n    \"\"\"Stands in for a @tool object: exposes .invoke(dict) -> str.\"\"\"\n    def __init__(self, fn, calls):\n        self._fn = fn\n        self._calls = calls\n\n    def invoke(self, arg):\n        self._calls.append(arg)\n        return self._fn(arg)\n\n\ndef success_page(url):\n    return f\"[FETCH STATUS: SUCCESS]\\nURL: {url}\\nTITLE: t\\nCONTENT:\\nrelevant page content for {url}\"\n\n\ndef failed_page(url):\n    return f\"[FETCH STATUS: FAILED]\\nURL: {url}\\nREASON: HTTP 403\"\n\n\nclass Patcher:\n    \"\"\"Monkeypatch app.main globals with restore-on-exit.\"\"\"\n    def __init__(self, **overrides):\n        self.overrides = overrides\n        self.saved = {}\n\n    def __enter__(self):\n        for k, v in self.overrides.items():\n            self.saved[k] = getattr(m, k)\n            setattr(m, k, v)\n        return self\n\n    def __exit__(self, *exc):\n        for k, v in self.saved.items():\n            setattr(m, k, v)\n\n\ndef run_auditor_with(claims, fetch_map, search_output, audit_fn, query=\"NEUTRAL QUERY about claim subject\"):\n    \"\"\"Runs m.auditor() with patched leaves. Returns (audit_results, updated_claims,\n    fetch_calls, search_calls, audit_calls).\"\"\"\n    fetch_calls, search_calls, audit_calls = [], [], []\n\n    fake_fetch = FakeTool(lambda a: fetch_map.get(a[\"url\"], failed_page(a[\"url\"])), fetch_calls)\n    fake_search = FakeTool(lambda a: search_output, search_calls)\n\n    def fake_audit(original_claim, evidence_url, fetched_data, is_fallback):\n        audit_calls.append({\"original_claim\": original_claim, \"evidence_url\": evidence_url,\n                            \"fetched_data\": fetched_data, \"is_fallback\": is_fallback})\n        return audit_fn(original_claim, evidence_url, fetched_data, is_fallback)\n\n    with Patcher(fetch_page=fake_fetch, web_search=fake_search,\n                 _build_fallback_query=lambda oc: query, _audit_fetched_evidence=fake_audit):\n        out = m.auditor({\"claims\": claims})\n    return out[\"audit_results\"], out[\"claims\"], fetch_calls, search_calls, audit_calls\n\n\nORIGINAL_CLAIM = \"In 2019, Microsoft fully acquired OpenAI for $1 billion, making OpenAI a wholly-owned Microsoft subsidiary.\"\n\n\ndef base_claim(source_url):\n    return {\"original_claim\": ORIGINAL_CLAIM, \"evidence\": \"snippet\", \"source_url\": source_url,\n            \"source_title\": \"T\", \"evidence_type\": \"search_snippet\", \"verification_status\": \"unverified\"}\n\n\n# --- Scenario 1: original fetch succeeds -> NO fallback, existing behavior ---\naudit_results, claims, fetches, searches, audits = run_auditor_with(\n    claims=[base_claim(\"https://cited-ok.com\")],\n    fetch_map={\"https://cited-ok.com\": success_page(\"https://cited-ok.com\")},\n    search_output=\"URL: https://should-not-be-used.com\\n\",\n    audit_fn=lambda oc, url, data, fb: (\"supported\", \"audited_supported\", \"cited page verifies\", \"\\\"quote\\\"\"),\n)\nr = audit_results[0]\ncheck(len(searches) == 0, \"S1 original-success: fallback web_search was NOT called\")\ncheck(r[\"verification_status\"] == \"audited_supported\" and r[\"verdict\"] == \"supported\", \"S1: verdict supported / audited_supported\")\ncheck(r[\"fallback_search_performed\"] is False, \"S1: fallback_search_performed = False\")\ncheck(r[\"original_fetch_status\"] == \"success\", \"S1: original_fetch_status = success\")\ncheck(r[\"final_evidence_source\"] == \"original_cited_source\", \"S1: final_evidence_source = original_cited_source\")\ncheck(r[\"fallback_source_url\"] is None, \"S1: fallback_source_url is None\")\ncheck(audits and audits[0][\"is_fallback\"] is False, \"S1: audit ran with is_fallback=False\")\ncheck(claims[0][\"verification_status\"] == \"audited_supported\", \"S1: claim verification_status updated\")\n\n\n# --- Scenario 2: original fails + fallback search/fetch succeeds -> fallback used ---\naudit_results, claims, fetches, searches, audits = run_auditor_with(\n    claims=[base_claim(\"https://blocked.com\")],\n    fetch_map={\"https://blocked.com\": failed_page(\"https://blocked.com\"),\n               \"https://alt-good.com\": success_page(\"https://alt-good.com\")},\n    search_output=\"Title: X\\nURL: https://alt-good.com\\nContent: c\\n\",\n    audit_fn=lambda oc, url, data, fb: (\"supported\", \"audited_supported\", \"fallback page verifies\", \"\\\"fallback quote\\\"\"),\n)\nr = audit_results[0]\ncheck(len(searches) == 1, \"S2 fallback: exactly ONE fallback search performed\")\ncheck(r[\"fallback_search_performed\"] is True, \"S2: fallback_search_performed = True\")\ncheck(r[\"original_fetch_status\"] == \"failed\", \"S2: original_fetch_status = failed\")\ncheck(r[\"fallback_source_url\"] == \"https://alt-good.com\", \"S2: fallback_source_url = the alternative source\")\ncheck(r[\"fallback_fetch_status\"] == \"success\", \"S2: fallback_fetch_status = success\")\ncheck(r[\"final_evidence_source\"] == \"fallback_source\", \"S2: final_evidence_source = fallback_source\")\ncheck(r[\"verification_status\"] == \"audited_supported\" and r[\"verdict\"] == \"supported\", \"S2: verdict from fallback evidence\")\ncheck(audits and audits[-1][\"is_fallback\"] is True, \"S2: audit ran with is_fallback=True\")\ncheck(audits[-1][\"evidence_url\"] == \"https://alt-good.com\", \"S2: audit evaluated the fallback URL\")\ncheck(audits[-1][\"fetched_data\"].startswith(\"[FETCH STATUS: SUCCESS]\"), \"S2: audit used the fetched fallback PAGE (not a snippet)\")\ncheck(claims[0][\"verification_status\"] == \"audited_supported\", \"S2: claim upgraded to audited_supported via fallback\")\n\n\n# --- Scenario 3: original fails + fallback fetch also fails -> UNSUPPORTED ---\naudit_results, claims, fetches, searches, audits = run_auditor_with(\n    claims=[base_claim(\"https://blocked.com\")],\n    fetch_map={\"https://blocked.com\": failed_page(\"https://blocked.com\"),\n               \"https://alt-bad.com\": failed_page(\"https://alt-bad.com\")},\n    search_output=\"URL: https://alt-bad.com\\n\",\n    audit_fn=lambda oc, url, data, fb: (\"supported\", \"audited_supported\", \"should not be called\", \"x\"),\n)\nr = audit_results[0]\ncheck(r[\"verdict\"] == \"unsupported\" and r[\"verification_status\"] == \"failed\", \"S3: original+fallback fail -> UNSUPPORTED/failed\")\ncheck(r[\"fallback_fetch_status\"] == \"failed\", \"S3: fallback_fetch_status = failed\")\ncheck(r[\"final_evidence_source\"] == \"none\", \"S3: final_evidence_source = none\")\ncheck(len(audits) == 0, \"S3: audit LLM NOT called when no page was successfully fetched\")\ncheck(str(r[\"supporting_evidence\"]).startswith(\"[FETCH STATUS: FAILED]\"), \"S3: supporting_evidence keeps the FAILED marker (a failed fetch is never supporting evidence)\")\n\n\n# --- Scenario 4: fallback source UNRELATED -> must NOT be CONTRADICTED merely for being unrelated ---\naudit_results, claims, fetches, searches, audits = run_auditor_with(\n    claims=[base_claim(\"https://blocked.com\")],\n    fetch_map={\"https://blocked.com\": failed_page(\"https://blocked.com\"),\n               \"https://unrelated.com\": success_page(\"https://unrelated.com\")},\n    search_output=\"URL: https://unrelated.com\\n\",\n    # A faithful audit of an unrelated page returns 'unsupported', not 'contradicted'.\n    audit_fn=lambda oc, url, data, fb: (\"unsupported\", \"failed\", \"page is unrelated to the claim\", \"n/a\"),\n)\nr = audit_results[0]\ncheck(r[\"verdict\"] == \"unsupported\", \"S4: unrelated fallback page -> verdict unsupported (NOT contradicted)\")\ncheck(r[\"verdict\"] != \"contradicted\", \"S4: unrelated fallback page is NOT marked contradicted\")\ncheck(r[\"fallback_fetch_status\"] == \"success\" and r[\"final_evidence_source\"] == \"fallback_source\",\n      \"S4: fallback fetch still recorded as a successful fetch even though verdict is unsupported\")\n\n\n# --- Scenario 5: fallback yields only a snippet (candidate fetch fails) -> never 'verified' ---\n# Same shape as S3 but framed as the fb: (\"supported\", \"audited_supported\", \"should not be called\", \"x\"),\n)\nr = audit_results[0]\ncheck(r[\"verification_status\"] not in (\"audited_supported\", \"audited_contradicted\"),\n      \"S5: fallback snippet without a successful page fetch is NEVER treated as verified evidence\")\ncheck(len(audits) == 0, \"S5: audit LLM not invoked on an unfetched snippet\")\n\n\n# --- Scenario 6: original claim preserved verbatim across every path ---\nfor label, ar in [(\"S1\", \"https://cited-ok.com\")]:\n    pass\n# Check across S1-S5 results collected above is implicit; do an explicit multi-claim run:\naudit_results, claims, _, _, _ = run_auditor_with(\n    claims=[base_claim(\"https://cited-ok.com\"), base_claim(\"https://blocked.com\")],\n    fetch_map={\"https://cited-ok.com\": success_page(\"https://cited-ok.com\"),\n               \"https://blocked.com\": failed_page(\"https://blocked.com\"),\n               \"https://alt-good.com\": success_page(\"https://alt-good.com\")},\n    search_output=\"URL: https://alt-good.com\\n\",\n    audit_fn=lambda oc, url, data, fb: (\"supported\", \"audited_supported\", \"ok\", \"\\\"q\\\"\"),\n)\ncheck(all(r[\"original_claim\"] == ORIGINAL_CLAIM for r in audit_results),\n      \"S6: original_claim preserved verbatim in every audit record\")\ncheck(all(c[\"original_claim\"] == ORIGINAL_CLAIM for c in claims),\n      \"S6: original_claim preserved verbatim in every updated claim\")\n\n\n# --- Unit: _extract_urls_from_search ---\nso = \"Title: A\\nURL: https://a.com\\nContent: c\\n\\nTitle: B\\nURL: https://b.com\\nContent: c\\n\\nURL: https://a.com\\n\"\nurls = m._extract_urls_from_search(so, exclude_url=\"https://a.com\")\ncheck(urls == [\"https://b.com\"], \"extract_urls: excludes the failed cited URL and dedups\")\nurls2 = m._extract_urls_from_search(so, exclude_url=None)\ncheck(urls2 == [\"https://a.com\", \"https://b.com\"], \"extract_urls: preserves order, dedups repeats\")\n\n\n# --- Prompt-level guards (real helpers, only llm.with_structured_output patched) ---\n\nclass CapturingStructured:\n    \"\"\"Captures the prompt passed to .invoke and returns a canned object.\"\"\"\n    def __init__(self, canned):\n        self.canned = canned\n        self.captured_prompt = None\n\n    def invoke(self, messages):\n        self.captured_prompt = messages[0].content\n        return self.canned\n\n\nclass _AR:  # minimal stand-in for an AuditRecord result\n    verdict = \"unsupported\"\n    reasoning = \"r\"\n ## 1. Files changed

- **`app/main.py`** — the only application-code change. Added:
  - `FallbackSearchQuery` Pydantic model (for neutral query generation).
  - Four module-level helpers: `_map_verdict_to_status`, `_extract_urls_from_search`, `_build_fallback_query`, `_audit_fetched_evidence`, plus `_assemble_audit_record`.
  - Rewrote the `auditor()` per-claim loop to add the fallback path and provenance fields (and one extra debug-print line).
  - `AuditRecord` model, Feedback, Analyst prompts, `compose_final_answer`, and memory were **not** changed.
- **`benchmark/run_benchmark.py`** — `count_auditor_fetches()` now prefers the new `original_fetch_status` field (backward-compatible, still returns exactly 3 keys); added `count_auditor_fallback_fetches()`; wired the 3 new fallback metrics into `run_question`, the console log, `run_question_safe`'s failure record, and `compute_summary` totals.
- **`benchmark/test_count_auditor_fallback_fetches.py`** *(new)* — fallback-counting fixture test.
- **`benchmark/test_auditor_fallback.py`** *(new)* — the core auditor fallback-flow fixture test.
- **`benchmark/BENCHMARK_SPEC.md`** — documented the new fallback metrics and test files.

**Not touched:** `app/research_memory.json` (still 28 lessons; its `M` in git is carried over from prior passes, not from this task), all five historical result files (unchanged mtimes), Feedback logic, Analyst prompts, `compose_final_answer`.

## 2. Fallback flow

Per claim, in `auditor()`:

1. **Fetch the Analyst's cited URL** (unchanged).
2. **On SUCCESS** → verify with the existing cited-source prompt and record; `fallback_search_performed=False`, `final_evidence_source="original_cited_source"`. **No fallback search happens** — existing behavior is preserved exactly.
3. **On FAILURE** → record `original_fetch_status="failed"`, then:
   a. Generate **one neutral, claim-oriented** search query via `_build_fallback_query` (LLM-based, with a banned-word guard — `true/false/debunked/hoax/confirmed/fake/myth` → rejected, falls back to the raw claim; never appends a truth assumption).
   b. Run **one** independent `web_search`, parse candidate URLs (excluding the failed cited URL, de-duplicated, rank-ordered).
   c. Fetch the **top candidate**.
   d. **Fallback fetch SUCCESS** → verify with a fallback-specific prompt whose rule 5 explicitly forbids `contradicted` when the page is unrelated/silent (requirement 6); `final_evidence_source="fallback_source"`, and the claim's `verification_status` is upgraded (e.g. to `audited_supported`/`audited_contradicted`).
   e. **Fallback fetch FAILS or no candidate** → `verdict="unsupported"`, `verification_status="failed"` (exactly as before); `supporting_evidence` keeps the `[FETCH STATUS: FAILED]` marker so a failed fetch is never used as supporting evidence.

Independence is preserved: the fallback search seeks evidence about the claim's *subject*, never the Analyst's conclusion; the audit LLM only ever runs on a **successfully fetched page**, never a snippet; and `source_url` in the record stays the original cited URL (so `compose_final_answer`'s per-claim join is unaffected), with the fallback URL in the separate `fallback_source_url` field. New provenance on every record: `original_source_url`, `original_fetch_status`, `fallback_search_performed`, `fallback_search_query`, `fallback_source_url`, `fallback_fetch_status`, `final_evidence_source`, `final_verdict`.

**Minor observation (no action taken):** `compose_final_answer` still labels this "source could not be independently fetched or verified" because `verification_status` collapses to `failed`. That wording is slightly imprecise now — a fallback page *was* fetched; it just didn't substantiate the claim. The Auditor's own reasoning field states this correctly ("The fetched fallback page provides Microsoft's 2025 Annual Report…"). I did not change `compose_final_answer` (not permitted this task, not required).

## 3. Q8 across Pass 1–4

| Pass | Cited source | Original fetch | Fallback | Verdict | Quality |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | `unanswered.io/…is-tableau-owned-by-salesforce` (**unrelated**) | succeeded | — | CONTRADICTED | right label, **wrong source** |
| P2 | Reuters MS-invests-$1B | **failed** | none | UNSUPPORTED | relevant source, unusable |
| P3 | Reuters MS-invests-$1B | **failed** | none | UNSUPPORTED | relevant source, unusable |
| **P4** | `crunchbase.com/…microsoft-commits-1-billion-to-openai-partnership` (**relevant**) | **succeeded** | not needed | **CONTRADICTED** | **right label, right source, right reason** |

**Reading:** P4 is the strongest Q8 result of all four passes — a genuinely relevant source (a Crunchbase article about the actual *$1B partnership*) fetched cleanly, and the Auditor correctly **CONTRADICTED** the "fully acquired / wholly-owned subsidiary" framing, distinguishing the real $1B investment/partnership from an acquisition.

**Honest caveat:** the fallback did **not** fire on Q8 this run — the Analyst happened to cite a fetchable, relevant source, so the original fetch succeeded. So Q8's improvement in P4 is attributable to Analyst source-selection variance (nondeterministic), **not** to the new fallback mechanism. The fallback was neither needed nor tested by Q8 here. And no unrelated fallback source was misclassified as a contradiction anywhere in Pass 4.

## 4. Overall S/C/U comparison

| Pass | Supported | Contradicted | Unsupported |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | 6 | 1 | 1 |
| P2 | 6 | 0 | 3 |
| P3 | 5 | 0 | 4 |
| **P4** | **6** | **1** | **1** |

P4 has the **fewest unsupported (1)**, down from 4 in P3, and restored a contradiction. But P1 also scored 6/1/1, so P4 matches the best prior pass rather than exceeding it.

## 5. Fallback usage statistics

- Fallback triggered on **2 of 8** questions (Q4, Q7) — precisely the two with a failed original fetch.
- **2 fallback searches, 2 fallback fetches, 2 successes, 0 failures.**
- **Q7 is the clean, causally-attributable win:** original source `facebook.com/…` failed → neutral fallback search `"Elon Musk OpenAI cofounder board departure 2018"` → fetched `businessinsider.com/…` → **SUPPORTED**. Under the old (pre-fallback) code this would have been UNSUPPORTED. The fallback directly rescued a real verification.
- Both fallback verdicts came only from **successfully fetched pages** (Q4→MS report, Q7→Business Insider); no snippet was ever treated as evidence.

## 6. Token / time impact

| | P3 (pre-fallback semantics for these Qs) | P4 |
|---|---|---|
| Total tokens | 147,055 | 157,988 (+7.4%) |
| Total elapsed | 124.5s | 156.3s |
| Q4 | 25.5s / 41,499 tok | 45.0s / 45,276 tok |
| Q7 | 32.9s / 13,845 tok | 17.8s / 15,649 tok |

The fallback adds one extra search + fetch + audit-LLM call, but **only on questions whose original fetch fails** — bounded overhead on 2 of 8 questions. The token increase (~+11k vs P3) is modest and localized. Q4's 45s is dominated by a 25.8s chatbot LLM call (latency variance), not the fallback itself (its fallback search+fetch was ~5s combined). Time totals are noisy across passes (P2 was 970s from unrelated latency spikes), so no strong time-trend claim is warranted.

## 7. Did the Auditor fallback demonstrably improve verification?

**Yes, with a precise scope:**

- **Demonstrated (Q7):** the fallback converted a hard fetch-failure dead-end into a genuine, fetched-evidence **SUPPORTED** verdict. This is directly attributable to the new code (original fetch failed → fallback fetched → verified).
- **Demonstrated correctness under insufficient evidence (Q4):** the fallback obtained accessible evidence but correctly returned UNSUPPORTED rather than fabricating a comparison — validating the "don't force a verdict from insufficient/unrelated evidence" guard on live data.
- **Not attributable to fallback (Q8):** Q8's improved CONTRADICTED verdict came from the Analyst citing a fetchable relevant source this run; the fallback didn't fire. So the fallback did **not** cause Q8's improvement, and I won't claim it did.
- **Aggregate (unsupported 4→1 vs P3):** partly the fallback (Q7) and partly nondeterministic source-selection luck (Q8, Q6). n=1 per pass with live search remains too noisy to attribute the whole aggregate shift to the fallback.

**Net:** the fallback is working as designed and produced at least one clean, attributable verification rescue (Q7) plus correct restraint on insufficient evidence (Q4), with bounded, localized cost. It did not regress any question. The deterministic fixture tests already cover the branches that live runs can't reliably trigger (both-fail → UNSUPPORTED, unrelated → not contradicted).

## 1. Files changed

- **`app/main.py`** — three minimal edits:
  - Added `MEMORY_MAX_LESSONS = 8` constant.
  - `add_lessons_to_memory`: keeps case-insensitive dedup, and now **stops appending once memory is at the cap** (over-cap non-duplicates are reported as not-added). Return signature unchanged.
  - `chatbot` injection: now sends **only the `lesson` text** (dropped the long `reason` field), sliced to the first `MEMORY_MAX_LESSONS`.
- **`app/research_memory.json`** — replaced the 34 accumulated lessons with **6 curated, entity-agnostic principles**.
- **`app/research_memory_archive.json`** *(new)* — preserves the previous 34 lessons for provenance/history (`{archived_from, archived_count: 34, lessons: [...]}`).
- **`benchmark/test_memory_cap.py`** *(new)* — fixture test for dedup + cap + injection representation.

No changes to Analyst/Auditor/Feedback logic beyond the memory representation. No new dependencies. No embeddings.

## 2. Before / after memory size

**34 → 6 lessons.** The 6 curated principles cover all 5 required themes plus one on source-priority:
1. Snippets are leads, not verified evidence — fetch the source first.
2. If a source is inaccessible, verify against an independent accessible alternative.
3. Verify each entity/sub-claim independently in multi-part/comparative questions.
4. Verify the *nature* of a claim (investment vs acquisition, partnership vs ownership), not just numbers/phrasing.
5. Don't force a verdict when fetched evidence doesn't actually address the claim → unverified.
6. Prefer primary sources, but fall back to a reputable secondary when primary is inaccessible, and label evidence by how it was obtained.

None reference specific entities or benchmark answers.

## 3. Before / after injected memory size

| | Format | Lessons injected | Chars | ~Tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before | `- lesson (Reason: reason)`, all 34 | 34 | 11,345 | ~2,836 |
| After | `- lesson` only, capped at 8 | 6 | 1,101 | ~275 |

**~90% reduction** per chatbot call (and it can no longer grow past the cap).

## 4. Tests passed

All pass, no API calls:

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_memory_cap.py` (new, 14 checks) | PASS |
| `test_count_auditor_fetches.py` | PASS |
| `test_timing_instrumentation.py` | PASS |
| `test_count_auditor_fallback_fetches.py` | PASS |
| `test_auditor_fallback.py` | PASS |
| `--dry-run` | PASS |

Confirmed: all 5 historical benchmark result files unchanged (same timestamps); Pass 4's own file untouched.

## 5. Exact behavior of the new memory mechanism

- **Load:** `load_memory()` reads the curated JSON (now 6 principles) unchanged.
- **Inject (Analyst/chatbot):** builds the prompt block from `lesson` text **only** — `f"- {lesson}"` per item — over the first `MEMORY_MAX_LESSONS (8)` entries. The auditor `reason` field stays in the file for provenance but is no longer sent to the Analyst.
- **Write (Feedback → `add_lessons_to_memory`):** a proposed lesson is added only if (a) its normalized text isn't already present (case/whitespace-insensitive dedup, as before) **and** (b) memory is below `MEMORY_MAX_LESSONS`. Once at 8, no further lessons are added — memory is hard-bounded. With 6 curated principles, the Feedback engine can still add at most 2 genuinely new principles before the cap freezes growth.
- **Provenance:** the prior 34 lessons live in `app/research_memory_archive.json`; curated entries carry `source_of_feedback: "curated"` (auditor-generated ones remain `"auditor"`), which is read tolerantly (nothing validates the loaded JSON against the `Literal`).

  "content": "# PS3 — Analyst + Auditor: A Self-Improving Research & Verification System\n\n## Problem\n\nLLM research agents routinely conflate three very different things: a search\nengine *finding* a claim, a page being *fetched*, and a claim being *verified*.\nA snippet that mentions a fact is not proof of that fact, an inaccessible URL is\nnot evidence, and a plausible-sounding answer can still be wrong. This project\nenforces one rule end-to-end:\n\n> **SEARCH FOUND IT ≠ FETCHED IT ≠ AUDITOR VERIFIED IT**\n\nThe system is a LangGraph state graph with two cooperating roles — an **Analyst**\nthat researches and an independent **Auditor** that verifies — plus a persistent\nfeedback memory that carries lessons forward. It is a working research harness,\nnot a finished or perfect product; its value is that it never overstates how well\na claim was verified.\n\n## Analyst\n\nThe Analyst (`chatbot` node) answers a research question using two tools:\n`web_search` (Tavily) and `fetch_page`. It preserves exact source URLs and\nlabels evidence by how it was obtained (search snippet vs. fetched page). It is\nfree to answer from snippets, but those are never treated as verified.\n\n## Auditor\n\nThe Auditor runs **after** the Analyst and **independently re-fetches the cited\nsource** for every extracted claim — it does not trust the Analyst's own fetch.\nIt issues a verdict of `supported`, `contradicted`, or `unsupported` based only\non the page content it fetched itself.\n\n**Auditor fallback:** if the cited source cannot be fetched, the Auditor performs\n**one bounded, neutral fallback web search** about the claim's subject (not about\nthe Analyst's conclusion), fetches the top accessible alternative, and verifies\nagainst that. If the fallback fetch also fails, the verdict stays `unsupported`.\nAn unrelated or insufficient fallback page is **not** turned into a contradiction.\n\n## Evidence verification\n\nEvidence status is structured, never inferred from prose or domain name:\n\n- `unverified` → *Information from Search Snippets*\n- `fetched` → *Information from Fetched Page Content*\n- `audited_supported` → *Auditor-verified evidence (SUPPORTED)*\n- `audited_contradicted` → *Auditor-verified evidence (CONTRADICTED)*\n- `failed` → *Unverified — source could not be independently verified*\n\nA failed fetch is never supporting evidence, and the user's original claim is\npreserved verbatim (never rewritten to match the evidence). **Unsupported claims\nremain unsupported when the evidence is insufficient** — the system declines to\nmanufacture a verdict rather than guessing.\n\n## Persistent feedback memory\n\nAfter auditing, a Feedback engine turns audit outcomes into durable research\nlessons (`Auditor → Feedback → Analyst`). Lessons persist across runs and are\ninjected into future Analyst prompts, so the system can adjust its research\nbehavior over time.\n\nThe raw memory grew to 34 lessons across four benchmark passes, mostly\nparaphrase duplicates. It was **compressed to 6 durable, entity-agnostic\nprinciples** with an **8-lesson runtime cap** and lesson-text-only injection.\nThis change reduced injected memory by roughly 90% (≈2,800 → ≈275 tokens per\nAnalyst call) and bounds future growth. **It was a cost/robustness change; we do\nnot claim it improved answer accuracy** — accuracy across passes is dominated by\nlive-search nondeterminism and was not attributable to memory changes.\n\n## Benchmark methodology\n\nA self-written 8-question benchmark (`benchmark/questions.json`) increases in\ndifficulty and reuses entities across questions (basic fact → multi-source →\nentity reuse → comparison → conflicting sources → multi-hop → hard verification →\nadversarial). Questions run **sequentially** so later questions can benefit from\nmemory written earlier. The harness (`benchmark/run_benchmark.py`) invokes the\nunmodified agent and records, per question: elapsed time, input/output/total\ntokens, searches, Analyst and Auditor fetches (including fallback), verdict\ncounts, lessons generated/added, memory size, and a per-node timing breakdown.\nToken usage and timing are captured via LangChain callbacks; no application code\nis modified for measurement. Deterministic fixture tests cover the branches that\nlive runs can't reliably trigger.\n\n## Cost tracking\n\nCosts are computed from `benchmark/pricing_config.json` using official list\nprices (verified 2026-09-26): Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite ($0.30 / 1M input, $2.50 / 1M\noutput) and Tavily basic search ($0.008 / credit), converted at USD→INR ≈ 96.\nThe harness reports per-question LLM/search/total cost in INR and the average\nacross the run; assumptions (paid tier, basic search depth, indicative FX rate,\nAnalyst-search-only cost basis) are documented in the config.\n\n## Key benchmark result (latest completed run — Pass 4)\n\n| Metric | Value |\n|---|---|\n| Questions completed | 8 / 8 |\n| Total time | 156.33 s |\n| Total tokens | 157,988 |\n| Analyst searches | 9 |\n| Auditor original fetches | 8 |\n| Auditor fallback searches | 2 |\n| Auditor fallback fetches | 2 (both succeeded) |\n| Supported / Contradicted / Unsupported | 6 / 1 / 1 |\n| Feedback lessons generated (before memory compression) | 6 |\n| Estimated cost | ≈ ₹13.00 total (≈ ₹1.63 / question) |\n\nIn this run the fallback rescued one claim whose cited source was unreachable\n(fetching an independent alternative and verifying it), and correctly left\nanother claim `unsupported` when the fallback evidence did not actually address\nthe comparison. These results reflect one live run with nondeterministic web\nsearch; they demonstrate the mechanism working, not a guarantee of accuracy.\n\n## Running\n\n```\npython -m benchmark.run_benchmark --dry-run          # structural check, no API calls\npython -m benchmark.run_benchmark --question 1        # one question, live\npython -m benchmark.run_benchmark --all --pass-id N   # full 8-question run\npython app/main.py                                     # interactive agent\n```\n\nRequires `GOOGLE_API_KEY` and `TAVILY_API_KEY` in `.env`. See `DECISIONS.md`,\n`STATUS.md`, and `HANDOFF.md` for architecture and history.\n"
}
````

  "content": "# DECISIONS.md\n\nArchitectural decisions for the PS3 Analyst + Auditor system, in the order they\nwere made. Kept intentionally short (≤ 2 pages).\n\n## 1. LangGraph state graph\nThe system is a single LangGraph `StateGraph`, not an ad-hoc loop. Flow:\n`chatbot → (tools ↔ chatbot) → extract_claims → auditor → feedback →\ncompose_final_answer → END`. A typed `State` carries messages, claims,\naudit_results, and feedback_lessons. Chosen for explicit, inspectable stages and\nbecause measurement (tokens/timing) attaches cleanly to named nodes.\n\n## 2. Search snippets are not evidence\nA `web_search` result is a lead, never verified evidence. Only a successfully\n`fetch_page`-d page counts as fetched content, and only an Auditor-fetched page\ncounts as verified. This rule (`SEARCH FOUND IT ≠ FETCHED IT ≠ AUDITOR VERIFIED\nIT`) is enforced structurally, not by prose.\n\n## 3. Analyst fetching vs. Auditor independent verification\nThe Analyst may answer from snippets or its own fetches, but the Auditor does\n**not** trust the Analyst's evidence. The Auditor independently re-fetches each\ncited source and judges only from what it fetched itself. Separating \"researcher\"\nfrom \"verifier\" is the core zero-trust design.\n\n## 4. Original claim preservation\nThe user's original factual claim is stored verbatim and never rewritten to match\nwhat the evidence says (the \"Satya Nadella 2010\" bug). Verdicts describe the\noriginal claim; they do not silently correct it.\n\n## 5. Persistent Auditor → Feedback → Analyst memory\nAudit outcomes feed a Feedback engine that writes durable research lessons to a\nJSON store, which is injected into future Analyst prompts. This is the\nself-improvement loop: verification failures become future guidance.\n\n## 6. Memory compression + runtime cap\nUnbounded append + exact-string dedup let the memory grow to 34 mostly-duplicate\nlessons (~2,800 injected tokens/call). We compressed it to **6 durable,\nentity-agnostic principles**, inject **lesson text only** (not the long audit\nreason), and enforced an **8-lesson hard cap** so it cannot grow without bound\n(~275 injected tokens/call). Prior lessons are archived for provenance. This is a\ncost/hygiene decision; we do **not** claim it improved accuracy.\n\n## 7. Auditor fallback search\nIf the cited source cannot be fetched, the Auditor runs **one bounded, neutral**\nfallback web search about the claim's *subject* (never \"claim is false\"), fetches\nthe top accessible alternative, and verifies against it. If the fallback fetch\nalso fails, the verdict stays `unsupported`. An unrelated/insufficient fallback\npage must yield `unsupported`, not a false `contradicted`. This removes the\nsingle-point-of-failure where one blocked URL killed verification.\n\n## 8. Deterministic final-answer composition after auditing\nThe user-facing answer is built by `compose_final_answer` **after** the Auditor\nruns, mapping structured `verification_status` to fixed evidence labels in code —\nnot by asking the LLM to describe its own confidence. This guarantees the final\nanswer's evidence labels match the verified state.\n\n## 9. Token / cost / timing instrumentation\nThe benchmark harness measures the unmodified agent externally via LangChain\ncallbacks: token usage, per-node timing (with an \"unaccounted\" residual), and\nAuditor original vs. fallback fetch counts. Cost is computed from a documented\n`pricing_config.json` (official Gemini + Tavily list prices, USD→INR ≈ 96),\nreporting per-question and average INR. No application code is changed for\nmeasurement.\n\n## 10. Why we stopped benchmarking after Pass 4\nPasses 1–3 established a baseline and exposed two problems: a fragile single-fetch\nAuditor and an unrelated-source false contradiction on the adversarial question.\nPass 4 validated the Auditor fallback (it rescued one blocked-source claim and\ncorrectly withheld a verdict when evidence was insufficient). With the fallback\nvalidated and memory compressed, further live passes would mostly re-measure\nnondeterministic web-search variance at real API cost without testing anything\nnew; deterministic fixture tests already cover the branch logic. So we froze the\narchitecture at Pass 4 and moved to finalization.\n"
}

```
1	# DECISIONS.md
2	
3	Architectural decisions for the PS3 Analyst + Auditor system, in the order they
4	were made. Kept intentionally short (≤ 2 pages).
5	
6	## 1. LangGraph state graph
7	The system is a single LangGraph `StateGraph`, not an ad-hoc loop. Flow:
8	`chatbot → (tools ↔ chatbot) → extract_claims → auditor → feedback →
9	compose_final_answer → END`. A typed `State` carries messages, claims,
10	audit_results, and feedback_lessons. Chosen for explicit, inspectable stages and
11	because measurement (tokens/timing) attaches cleanly to named nodes.
12	
13	## 2. Search snippets are not evidence
14	A `web_search` result is a lead, never verified evidence. Only a successfully
15	`fetch_page`-d page counts as fetched content, and only an Auditor-fetched page
16	counts as verified. This rule (`SEARCH FOUND IT ≠ FETCHED IT ≠ AUDITOR VERIFIED
17	IT`) is enforced structurally, not by prose.
18	
19	## 3. Analyst fetching vs. Auditor independent verification
20	The Analyst may answer from snippets or its own fetches, but the Auditor does
21	**not** trust the Analyst's evidence. The Auditor independently re-fetches each
22	cited source and judges only from what it fetched itself. Separating "researcher"
23	from "verifier" is the core zero-trust design.
24	
25	## 4. Original claim preservation
26	The user's original factual claim is stored verbatim and never rewritten to match
27	what the evidence says (the "Satya Nadella 2010" bug). Verdicts describe the
28	original claim; they do not silently correct it.
29	
30	## 5. Persistent Auditor → Feedback → Analyst memory
31	Audit outcomes feed a Feedback engine that writes durable research lessons to a
32	JSON store, which is injected into future Analyst prompts. This is the
33	self-improvement loop: verification failures become future guidance.
34	
35	## 6. Memory compression + runtime cap
36	Unbounded append + exact-string dedup let the memory grow to 34 mostly-duplicate
37	lessons (~2,800 injected tokens/call). We compressed it to **6 durable,
38	entity-agnostic principles**, inject **lesson text only** (not the long audit
39	reason), and enforced an **8-lesson hard cap** so it cannot grow without bound
40	(~275 injected tokens/call). Prior lessons are archived for provenance. This is a
41	cost/hygiene decision; we do **not** claim it improved accuracy.
42	
43	## 7. Auditor fallback search
44	If the cited source cannot be fetched, the Auditor runs **one bounded, neutral**
45	fallback web search about the claim's *subject* (never "claim is false"), fetches
46	the top accessible alternative, and verifies against it. If the fallback fetch
47	also fails, the verdict stays `unsupported`. An unrelated/insufficient fallback
48	page must yield `unsupported`, not a false `contradicted`. This removes the
49	single-point-of-failure where one blocked URL killed verification.
50	
51	## 8. Deterministic final-answer composition after auditing
52	The user-facing answer is built by `compose_final_answer` **after** the Auditor
53	runs, mapping structured `verification_status` to fixed evidence labels in code —
54	not by asking the LLM to describe its own confidence. This guarantees the final
55	answer's evidence labels match the verified state.
56	
57	## 9. Token / cost / timing instrumentation
58	The benchmark harness measures the unmodified agent externally via LangChain
59	callbacks: token usage, per-node timing (with an "unaccounted" residual), and
60	Auditor original vs. fallback fetch counts. Cost is computed from a documented
61	`pricing_config.json` (official Gemini + Tavily list prices, USD→INR ≈ 96),
62	reporting per-question and average INR. No application code is changed for
63	measurement.
64	
65	## 10. Why we stopped benchmarking after Pass 4
66	Passes 1–3 established a baseline and exposed two problems: a fragile single-fetch
67	Auditor and an unrelated-source false contradiction on the adversarial question.
68	Pass 4 validated the Auditor fallback (it rescued one blocked-source claim and
69	correctly withheld a verdict when evidence was insufficient). With the fallback
70	validated and memory compressed, further live passes would mostly re-measure
71	nondeterministic web-search variance at real API cost without testing anything
72	new; deterministic fixture tests already cover the branch logic. So we froze the
73	architecture at Pass 4 and moved to finalization.
74	
```

148	    cited-source fetches (count_auditor_fetches above). A fallback fetch is attempted
149	    only when the original cited-source fetch failed AND the fallback search returned a
150	    usable candidate URL. Success/failure is read from the explicit provenance field
151	    'fallback_fetch_status' ('success'/'failed'/'no_results'/None) added by auditor().
152	
153	    Records that predate the fallback upgrade have no fallback fields; they contribute 0
154	    to every count (via .get defaults), so this is safe on old-shape audit_results too.
155	    """
156	    attempted = 0
157	    successful = 0
158	    failed = 0
159	    for a in audit_results:
160	        status = a.get("fallback_fetch_status")
161	        if status == "success":
162	            attempted += 1
163	            successful += 1
164	        elif status == "failed":
165	            attempted += 1
166	            failed += 1
167	        # "no_results" (search returned nothing to fetch) or None (no fallback / old
168	        # record) are not counted as fallback fetch attempts.
169	    return {
170	        "auditor_fallback_fetches": attempted,
171	        "auditor_fallback_successful_fetches": successful,
172	        "auditor_fallback_failed_fetches": failed,
173	    }
174	
```

Create a virtual environment and install dependencies\npython -m venv .venv\n# Windows:        .venv\\Scripts\\activate\n# macOS / Linux:  source .venv/bin/activate\npip install -r requirements.txt\n\n# 3. So we froze the\narchitecture at Pass 4 and moved to finalization.\n\n## Rejected / replaced alternatives\n- **Prompt-only evidence labelling** (ask the LLM to state its own confidence):\n  measured in early Phase 6.1 and rejected — the model mislabelled search\n  snippets as \"fetched/verified\". Replaced by deterministic status→label mapping\n  in `compose_final_answer` (decision 8).\n- **Unbounded append-only memory with exact-string dedup**: measured across\n  Passes 1–4; it grew to 34 near-duplicate lessons and inflated the prompt.\n  Replaced by 6 curated principles + 8-lesson cap (decision 6).\n- **Single-fetch Auditor** (no fallback): rejected after Q4/Q8 in Passes 1–3\n  showed one blocked URL killing verification. Replaced by the bounded fallback\n  (decision 7).\n- **Vector/embedding memory**: rejected as over-engineered for a hackathon; a\n  small JSON principle set is enough and adds no dependency.\n\n## Trade-offs under the time limit\n- Benchmark runs are single-trial per pass (n=1); live-search nondeterminism is\n  not averaged out, so we report trends cautiously and lean on deterministic\n  fixture tests for correctness.\n- The fallback tries **one** neutral search + top result, not an exhaustive\n  multi-source sweep — cheaper and bounded, at the cost of occasionally missing a\n  usable source deeper in the results.\n- Cost is computed post-hoc from token/search counts (list prices + indicative\n  FX), not from real billing.\n\n## Testing\nSeven offline fixture suites (no API cost) cover: original vs. fallback fetch\ncounting, the fallback control-flow (success / both-fail / unrelated→unsupported /\nsnippet-never-verified), NO-CITATION flagging, memory dedup+cap, cost math, and\ncallback timing attribution. A `--dry-run` validates graph structure and config.\nFull live behaviour was exercised across Passes 1–4 (results under\n`benchmark/results/`).\n\n## Where it breaks (known weaknesses + Auditor limitations)\n- **Full per-question trace is not persisted** to the result JSON (only metrics,\n  a 500-char answer excerpt, and per-op timing). The rich trace exists only in\n  run-time stdout. This is the biggest evaluation-readiness gap.\n- **No explicit Analyst \"plan\" step** and no explicit single-source cross-check\n  instruction; the ReAct loop reasons implicitly and the Auditor's independent\n  re-fetch is the de-facto second check.\n- Auditor verdict quality depends on the LLM judging one fetched page; a\n  correct-but-shallow page can yield `unsupported`. Fallback fetches are not\n  added to the Tavily cost figure. n=1 benchmarking limits accuracy claims.\n\n## With two more weeks\nPersist the full per-question trace (plan, every tool call + result, fallback,\nverdicts+reasoning, feedback, full answer) to a human-readable artifact; add an\nexplicit Analyst planning node and single-source cross-check; run each question\nN≥3× to separate real learning from search noise; broaden the fallback to a small\nmulti-source sweep; and fold Auditor fallback searches into the cost model."

  "new_string": "def serialize_message(msg):\n    \"\"\"Serialize one LangChain message (or dict) into a plain JSON-able record,\n    preserving role, text content, tool calls, and tool-result linkage so the\n    Analyst plan, every tool call, and every tool result survive into the trace.\n    Uses structured fields, never str(msg).\"\"\"\n    mtype = getattr(msg, \"type\", None) or (msg.get(\"type\") if isinstance(msg, dict) else None)\n    content = getattr(msg, \"content\", None)\n    if content is None and isinstance(msg, dict):\n        content = msg.get(\"content\")\n    # content may be a string or a list of structured blocks\n    if isinstance(content, list):\n        text = \"\\n\".join(\n            b.get(\"text\", \"\") if isinstance(b, dict) else str(b)\n            for b in content\n        )\n    else:\n        text = content if isinstance(content, str) else (\"\" if content is None else str(content))\n    rec = {\"role\": mtype, \"content\": text}\n    tool_calls = getattr(msg, \"tool_calls\", None)\n    if tool_calls:\n        rec[\"tool_calls\"] = [\n            {\"name\": tc.get(\"name\"), \"args\": tc.get(\"args\")} if isinstance(tc, dict) else str(tc)\n            for tc in tool_calls\n        ]\n    name = getattr(msg, \"name\", None)\n    if name:\n        rec[\"name\"] = name  # e.g. the tool that produced a ToolMessage\n    return rec\n\n\ndef build_trace(final_state, final_answer_full):\n    \"\"\"Assemble the full, evaluator-readable per-question trace from graph state.\n    Contains: the Analyst message history (plan + every tool call + tool result),\n    the structured claims, the Auditor audit_results (verdicts, reasoning,\n    supporting evidence, citation_status, and fallback provenance incl. the\n    fallback search query / URL / status), the feedback lessons, and the full\n    final answer. Fallback-after-failure is captured inside audit_results'\n    provenance fields rather than the message list, since the Auditor's fallback\n    search/fetch happen outside the graph's message channel.\"\"\"\n    return {\n        \"analyst_messages\": [serialize_message(m) for m in final_state.get(\"messages\", [])],\n        \"claims\": final_state.get(\"claims\", []),\n        \"audit_results\": final_state.get(\"audit_results\", []),\n        \"feedback_lessons\": final_state.get(\"feedback_lessons\", []),\n        \"final_answer_full\": final_answer_full,\n    }\n\n\ndef run_question(question: dict, pricing: dict, pass_id: int = 1) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Runs exactly one question through the real, unmodified agent and\n    returns its metric record. Makes real API calls (Gemini + Tavily)."
}

class State(TypedDict):
    # `add_messages` appends new messages to the existing list rather than overwriting them
    messages: Annotated[list, add_messages]
    claims: list[dict]
    audit_results: list[dict]
    feedback_lessons: list[dict]

=== audit record + claim fields the UI can render ===
def auditor(state: State):
    """Independently evaluates each extracted Analyst claim by re-inspecting cited sources.

    Robustness upgrade: if the Analyst's cited URL cannot be fetched, the Auditor performs
    ONE independent, neutral fallback web search about the original claim's subject, selects
    the top alternative accessible result, fetches it, and verifies against that fallback
    evidence. If the fallback fetch also fails (or no candidate is found), the verdict is
    UNSUPPORTED exactly as before. Successful cited-source fetches keep the prior behaviour
    unchanged (no fallback search is performed)."""
    claims = state.get("claims", [])
    if not claims:
        return {"audit_results": [], "claims": []}

    audit_results = []
    updated_claims = []

    for claim in claims:
        claim_copy = dict(claim)
        original_claim = claim_copy.get("original_claim", "")
        source_url = claim_copy.get("source_url", "")
        evidence_type = claim_copy.get("evidence_type", "search_snippet")
```

## ASSISTANT  ·  `2026-09-26T09:55:47`

Inspection is done. Here's what I found and what I'll build.

**Findings**
- The compiled graph is `chatbot ⇄ tools → extract_claims → auditor → feedback → compose_final_answer`. `agent.stream(..., stream_mode="updates")` yields one real event per completed node. Each update carries what the UI needs: tool calls with queries, tool results, claims, audit records (verdict, reasoning, `citation_status`, fallback provenance), feedback lessons, and the composed final answer.
- **`app/main.py` needs no change.** It's already invocable without the CLI (the `__main__` guard is intact), and the benchmark already imports `agent` the same way.
- Streamlit is not installed. A dry-run shows it installs on the venv's Python 3.14 (it pulls numpy, pandas, and pyarrow).
- Failure signals are already observable. `web_search` returns strings starting with `Error…` or `No results found.`. `fetch_page` returns `[FETCH STATUS: FAILED]`. The Auditor's record carries `original_fetch_status`, the fallback fields, and `citation_status`.
- One thing to know: a UI run executes the real Feedback node. It can append to `app/research_memory.json` if there is room under the 8-lesson cap, and memory is currently full at 8. The UI writes no benchmark files.

**Plan**
1. **Where it lives:** a new top-level `ui/` package, separate from `app/` and `benchmark/`.
2. **How it invokes the workflow:** `ui/runner.py` calls the existing `app.main.agent.stream(..., stream_mode="updates")` and yields `(node, update)` pairs. `ui/events.py` turns those into trace events and stage states. Nothing is faked, and errors surface as failed events.
3. **Files to add:**
   - `ui/events.py`: pure logic, no Streamlit, no app import.
   - `ui/render.py`: HTML and CSS builders, with all dynamic text escaped.
   - `ui/runner.py`: the thin wrapper over the existing agent.
   - `ui/streamlit_app.py`: the page.
   - `ui/requirements-ui.txt`: Streamlit only, so core `requirements.txt` stays untouched.
   - `.streamlit/config.toml`: dark theme.
   - `ui/test_ui_events.py`, `ui/test_ui_app.py`, `ui/test_ui_integration.py`.
4. **Files to change:** `README.md` only, adding a Demo UI section.

I'll start with the pure event logic.

  "content": "\"\"\"\nThin bridge between the demo UI and the EXISTING Analyst + Auditor workflow.\n\nIt does not duplicate any research logic: it imports the already-compiled\n`app.main.agent` and streams it with LangGraph's `stream_mode=\"updates\"`, yielding\none (node, update) pair as each real graph node completes. The UI reads results\nonly from these real updates.\n\nThis module never writes benchmark result files.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nREPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))\nif REPO_ROOT not in sys.path:\n    sys.path.insert(0, REPO_ROOT)\n\n\ndef missing_api_keys() -> list:\n    \"\"\"Names of required API keys not present in the environment (after .env load).\"\"\"\n    from dotenv import load_dotenv\n    load_dotenv(os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, \".env\"))\n    return [k for k in (\"GOOGLE_API_KEY\", \"TAVILY_API_KEY\") if not os.environ.get(k)]\n\n\ndef stream_research(question: str):\n    \"\"\"Run the existing agent on `question`, yielding (node_name, update_dict) as each\n    graph node finishes. Sequential, real, unmodified workflow.\"\"\"\n    from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage\n    from app.main import agent\n\n    for chunk in agent.stream({\"messages\": [HumanMessage(content=question)]}, stream_mode=\"updates\"):\n        for node, update in chunk.items():\n            yield node, update\n\n\ndef get_memory_view() -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Snapshot of persistent research memory as the Analyst will see it:\n    the concise lesson text only, capped at MEMORY_MAX_LESSONS.\"\"\"\n    from app.main import load_memory, MEMORY_MAX_LESSONS\n\n    lessons = [m.get(\"lesson\", \"\") for m in load_memory() if m.get(\"lesson\")]\n    return {\n        \"lessons\": lessons,\n        \"count\": len(lessons),\n        \"cap\": MEMORY_MAX_LESSONS,\n        \"injected\": min(len(lessons), MEMORY_MAX_LESSONS),\n    }\n\n\ndef get_evidence_label(verification_status: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The system's own deterministic evidence label for a verification_status.\"\"\"\n    from app.main import get_evidence_label as _label\n    return _label(verification_status)\n"
}

unsafe_allow_html=True)\nmetrics_ph = st.empty()\n\n\ndef paint(run, live=False):\n    \"\"\"Render every panel from the current run state (real data only).\"\"\"\n    statuses = run.stage_statuses() if run else {k: \"idle\" for k in ev.STAGES}\n    flow_ph.markdown(rd.flow_html(statuses), unsafe_allow_html=True)\n    trace_ph.markdown(\n        rd.trace_html(run.events if run else [], run.running if (run and live) else None,\n                      run.error if run else None),\n        unsafe_allow_html=True)\n    final_ph.markdown(rd.final_html(run, safe_label), unsafe_allow_html=True)\n    with composed_ph.container():\n        if run and run.final_answer:\n            with st.expander(\"Full composed answer\"):\n                st.markdown(run.final_answer)\n    view = safe_memory_view()\n    new = [l.get(\"lesson\", \"\") for l in run.feedback_lessons] if run else []\n    memory_ph.markdown(rd.memory_html(view, new), unsafe_allow_html=True)\n    metrics_ph.markdown(rd.metrics_html(ss[\"history\"], view[\"count\"]), unsafe_allow_html=True)\n\n\nif run_clicked:\n    q = (question or \"\").strip()\n    if not q:\n        st.warning(\"Enter a research question first.\")\n        paint(ss[\"last_run\"])\n    elif missing_keys:\n        st.error(\"Cannot run: missing \" + \", \".join(missing_keys) + \".\")\n        paint(ss[\"last_run\"])\n    else:\n        run = ev.RunState(q)\n        ss[\"last_run\"] = run\n        header_ph.markdown(rd.header_html(\"running\"), unsafe_allow_html=True)\n        paint(run, live=True)\n        try:\n            for node, update in runner.stream_research(q):\n                run.apply(node, update)\n                paint(run, live=True)\n        except Exception as exc:  # surfaced as a failed run, never as a success\n            run.fail(f\"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}\")\n        ss[\"history\"].append(rd.run_summary(run))\n        header_ph.markdown(rd.header_html(\"error\" if run.error else \"ready\"), unsafe_allow_html=True)\n        paint(run)\nelse:\n    last = ss[\"last_run\"]\n    if last is not None and not last.finished and not last.error:\n        last.fail(\"The run was interrupted before it finished.\")\n    paint(last)\n"

\"final_evidence_source\": \"original_cited_source\", \"final_verdict\": verdict,\n    }\n    rec.update(over)\n    return rec\n\n\ndef claim_record(status=\"audited_contradicted\", **over):\n    c = {\"original_claim\": DEMO_CLAIM, \"evidence\": \"snippet\", \"source_url\": SRC, \"source_title\": \"Example\",\n         \"evidence_type\": \"search_snippet\", \"verification_status\": status}\n 2019 investment details.\",\n        tool_calls=[{\"name\": \"web_search\", \"args\": {\"query\": query}, \"id\": \"c1\"}])]})\n\n\ndef _search_result(content=SEARCH_OK):\n    return (\"tools\", audit, claim_record(\"failed\"), [], \"## Final Verified Answer\\n\\nunverified\")\n\n\ndef fallback_supported_run():\n    audit = audit_record(\n        \"supported\", fallback_search_performed=True, fallback_search_query=\"q\")\n    return [_search_turn(), _search_result()] + _tail(\n        audit, claim_record(\"failed\", source_url=\"\"), [], \"## Final Verified It duplicates no research\nlogic, fakes no results, and never writes benchmark result files.\n\n```bash\n# install the UI dependency (kept separate from the core requirements)\npip install -r ui/requirements-ui.txt\n\n# start it from the repo root (needs the same .env keys as the rest of the project)\nstreamlit run ui/streamlit_app.py\n```\n\nThen open the printed local URL (default http://localhost:8501). ## ASSISTANT  ·  `2026-09-26T10:08:32`

The demo UI is built and works end-to-end against the real system. It's a Streamlit page in a new `ui/` package that calls the existing compiled `app.main.agent` and renders each real node result as it completes. Nothing was committed or pushed.

## What I built

**Where it lives and how it works**
- **`ui/runner.py`** streams the existing agent with `stream_mode="updates"`, so each completed graph node produces one real event.
- **`app/main.py` needed no changes.** Its 11-line diff is the earlier, still-uncommitted NO_CITATION change from the audit, not this task.
- **The trace shows only observable events:** tool names, queries, result counts, fetch outcomes, claims, Auditor fallback steps, verdicts and feedback. It shows no chain-of-thought; thinking blocks are dropped and there's a test for it.
- **The layout makes the structure obvious:** the workflow strip shows two agents and a feedback loop as separate colour-coded groups.

**Files added:**
- `ui/events.py`, `ui/render.py`, `ui/runner.py`, `ui/streamlit_app.py`
- `ui/requirements-ui.txt` (Streamlit only, so core `requirements.txt` is untouched)
- `.streamlit/config.toml` (dark theme)
- `ui/sample_updates.py` (test fixtures)
- `ui/test_ui_events.py`, `ui/test_ui_app.py`, `ui/test_ui_integration.py`

**File changed:** `README.md`, with a new "Demo UI" section. The Quickstart is untouched.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Existing backend tests (8) + `--dry-run` | ✅ all pass |
| UI event/render tests | ✅ pass |
| UI app tests (real page started headlessly, button clicked) | ✅ pass |
| Integration test (request → real compiled graph, only LLM/network faked) | ✅ pass |
| Real server serves the page | ✅ health 200 |

**Requirement coverage**
- **Renders verdicts:** SUPPORTED, UNSUPPORTED and CONTRADICTED are covered.
- **Renders failures:** "Search failed", "Source could not be independently verified", NO CITATION, a backend exception, and missing API keys.
- **Memory panel:** shows "8 lessons retained" and "Lessons injected into Analyst: 8".
- **Metrics:** shown; a failed run isn't counted as completed.

**What I saw in a real browser:** I drove headless Chrome and screenshotted three states plus a phone-width layout, which is how I caught two issues:
- Literal `###` and `**` showed up in the pre-audit draft preview.
- The Final Answer panel showed "UNAUDITED" while the Auditor was still working.

I fixed both. The panel now reads "AWAITING AUDIT" until the audit finishes, and tests cover both fixes. Phone width wraps and stacks cleanly.

**One live run:** I ran the default demo question once through the browser, using real Gemini and Tavily calls at roughly ₹1.5. The Auditor opened Wikipedia and returned **CONTRADICTED** (OpenAI is owned by employees and investors 47%, Microsoft 27%, the Foundation 26%). All seven stages completed. `research_memory.json` was byte-identical afterwards, and no benchmark file was created.

## Things to know

1. **The demo won't show a lesson being added.** Memory is at its 8-lesson cap, so Feedback truthfully shows "No new lesson added to memory". The learning loop is only visible as the stored lessons and the injected count. If you want a lesson visibly added on stage, trim memory before demoing, or raise the cap. I left both alone; it's your call.
2. **There's no visible plan text.** Gemini returned no prose alongside its tool call, so the trace shows "Chose tool(s): web_search". I don't invent a plan; when the Analyst does emit text, it's shown.
3. **Updates arrive per node, not per token.** You see each stage complete in sequence, which is the sequential visualization you allowed.
4. **The venv now has Streamlit**, plus numpy, pandas and pyarrow, which it pulls in. It installs cleanly on Python 3.14.
5. **A UI run can write memory.** If memory is below the cap, the real Feedback node adds lessons to `app/research_memory.json`, and each run makes real API calls. The README says both.
